# CLI Workflows

The `cli/` package installs the `nfn` command for training, inference,
evaluation, and backend diagnostics outside the web editor. It is an in-repo companion to the Python SDK:
it builds real `ModelSpec` objects, exports graph JSON plus `.pt` weights, uses
the shared dataset manager, and defaults artifacts to `~/NeuralFn/artifacts`.

For the longer operator runbook, see [../cli/README.md](../cli/README.md).

## Migrate a graph to Native Execution IR

Use the lightweight migration command to preflight a graph and lower its
resolved topology to Native Execution IR v1:

```bash
nfn migrate graph-to-native \
  --graph artifacts/model.json \
  --output-dir artifacts/model-native \
  --dry-run
```

The dry run prints a manifest and compatibility report as JSON and writes
nothing. `--output-dir` is still required and must not already exist. Remove
`--dry-run` to create a new artifact directory, or add an optional legacy `.pt`
checkpoint:

```bash
nfn migrate graph-to-native \
  --graph artifacts/model.json \
  --weights artifacts/model.pt \
  --output-dir artifacts/model-native

nfn migrate graph-to-native \
  --graph artifacts/model.json \
  --weights artifacts/model_00020000.bin \
  --output-dir artifacts/model-resident

nfn migrate graph-to-native \
  --graph artifacts/gpt2-moa.json \
  --weights artifacts/model_00020000.moa.json \
  --output-dir artifacts/gpt2-moa-resident

nfn migrate graph-to-native \
  --graph artifacts/llama.json \
  --weights artifacts/llama_native_family_model_00000000.json \
  --output-dir artifacts/llama-resident
```

Graph-only migration does not import Torch, NumPy, or NetworkX. Graph structure, builtin lowerer
coverage, custom-function rejection, and variant resolution are checked before
the optional checkpoint is opened. `.pt` conversion uses an isolated
`weights_only` worker and produces a 64-byte-aligned generic `weights.bin` with
per-tensor hashes. Compatible dense-v5 `.bin` input stays Torch-free, is
inspected against the graph, fingerprinted, and copied as owner-only
`model.bin` with a ready resident ABI. Canonical `llama` inference-checkpoint
v2 metadata is also inspected Torch-free; its exact contiguous float32 sidecar
is copied as `model.f32`. Direct `.f32` and diagnostic family metadata are
rejected. Existing destinations/symlinks are refused; source graph
bytes are never rewritten. Compatible results exit 0. Incompatible results
exit 2, include stable unsupported node paths, and do not create output.

For `gpt2_moa`, pass the source-bound `model_XXXXXXXX.moa.json`, not its bare
dense-v5 `.bin`. It must sit beside the matching `.bin` and empty
`DONE_XXXXXXXX`, bind the byte-identical graph and model hashes, and record the
canonical GELU/ReLU/SiLU/ReLU2 candidates, selected activation, and positive
selection interval. Migration retains that selection contract and copies the
validated model as `model.bin`.

The current registry structurally lowers all 67 shipped text presets. That is
not an all-family resident-runtime claim. Seven reviewed dense-v5 presets
(`gpt2`, megakernel, MoA, z-loss, QK-norm, stable, and softcap) have resident
sessions, lossless retained K/V cache, and lean serving proof. Canonical
`llama` additionally has a real float32 RMSNorm/RoPE/GQA/SwiGLU resident
forward and lossless cache; tokenizer-free `--prompt-tokens` uses that path,
while text/HTTP use still needs supported presentation metadata. Exact MoA
also supports the packed CPU TurboQuant cache for even head dimensions; its
training-time candidates are not reprobed during inference. Generic `.pt`,
graph-only, differential/modern variants, bare MoA `.bin` files, and every other family remain
closed. Compatible reviewed-dense artifacts with even head dimensions also
support explicit native packed CPU TurboQuant. Compatible artifacts separately
expose an opt-in hybrid Tile-CUDA attention backend through
`--turboquant-attention-backend tile-cuda --tile-ops-lib PATH`, while CPU stays
the default and other families remain unavailable. See
[Native Execution IR](python-sdk/native-ir.md) for artifact and SDK details.

### Muse Glimmer conversion and inference

Muse Glimmer uses strict pinned family conversion rather than generic `.pt`
migration:

```bash
nfn migrate muse-glimmer-to-native \
  --source /models/Muse-Glimmer-30B \
  --component full \
  --output-dir artifacts/glimmer-bf16

nfn migrate muse-glimmer-gguf-to-native \
  --gguf /models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-17GB-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --gguf /models/Muse-Glimmer-30B-KQuant-Dynamic-Q4_K_XL.gguf \
  --dflash /models/dflash-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --mmproj /models/mmproj-Muse-Glimmer-30B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --tokenizer-source /models/Muse-Glimmer-30B \
  --output-dir artifacts/glimmer-kquant
```

Run target-only or DFlash generation through the same one-shot and server
surfaces:

```bash
nfn infer \
  --checkpoint artifacts/glimmer-kquant \
  --runtime native-cuda \
  --weight-precision auto \
  --speculative-decoding auto \
  --companion-checkpoint dflash \
  --tile-ops-lib /absolute/path/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so \
  --prompt "Hello" \
  --native-info
```

`--weight-precision` accepts `auto`, `bf16`, `k-quant-dynamic`, or
`k-quant-17gb`. CUDA `auto` chooses quality-first only after current free-VRAM,
context/session cache, companion, staging, workspace, and reserve accounting.
An explicit value never downgrades and is not rejected merely because a
higher-quality profile could fit: `--weight-precision k-quant-17gb` remains a
valid pin on a 32-GB card when its measured budget fits. `--speculative-decoding` accepts `off`,
`auto`, or `required`; `required` fails rather than using target-only decode.
The precision/speculation choices are server startup policy and cannot be
overridden in a request body.

For whole-model CUDA, `--strict-tile-ops-lib PATH` is an alias of
`--tile-ops-lib PATH`. Both feed `NativeModelLoadConfig.tile_ops_lib`; the
former makes the strict-sidecar purpose explicit and now works on the exact
Native Execution artifact dispatch path as advertised by top-level help.
The accepted strict sidecar uses measured packed-projection/RMS→MMVQ
megakernels, DFlash packed-weight hoisting, verifier projection overlap,
direct transactional K/V staging, short-context attention splitting, and an
exact cooperative multirow dual-RMS megakernel. The final current-source run
measured 271.244 DFlash tok/s median; disabling only the cooperative RMS in the
same binary measured 264.724 tok/s with identical output and acceptance.
Their exact controls, hashes, memory, and RTX 5090 distributions are recorded in
[Resident Native Artifact CLI Inference](native-cli-inference.md); launch
reduction alone is not used as an acceptance criterion.

Attach a native LoRA or QLoRA result only after its base/tokenizer/template
lineage has been authenticated:

```bash
nfn migrate muse-glimmer-lora-to-native \
  --artifact artifacts/glimmer-bf16 \
  --checkpoint runs/glimmer-adapter/checkpoint-step-100
```

The command copies and publishes the adapter atomically, refuses overwrite,
and reports its training mode and CPU/CUDA resident capability. A stock DFlash
assistant is disabled for an adapted target unless a separately compatible
assistant is bound.

### Native Muse Glimmer training

`nfn train --base-model muse-glimmer` dispatches directly to the dedicated
Torch-free `nfn_muse_glimmer_native_train` binary. Use exact binary options for
the pinned BF16 source and uint32/structured-SFT dataset:

```bash
nfn train --base-model muse-glimmer \
  --checkpoint artifacts/glimmer-bf16/muse-glimmer-full.bf16 \
  --checkpoint-sha256 SHA256 \
  --dataset datasets/glimmer-sft \
  --objective sft \
  --chat-template-sha256 cfc67e5f349f37690dfd31ed1f18bc4442a9dd32fe39a648f993cb4eb3cae678 \
  --adapter qlora \
  --lora-targets q_proj,k_proj,v_proj,o_proj,attn_gate_proj,gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj \
  --lora-rank 8 --lora-alpha 16 --qlora-group-size 64 \
  --sequence-length 2048 --batch-size 1 --max-steps 100 \
  --tile-ops-lib /absolute/path/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so \
  --output-dir runs/glimmer-qlora
```

`--objective ar` consumes versioned uint32 shards. `--objective sft` consumes
structured `.sft` records with targets, loss masks, boundaries, and exact ATEM
lineage. DPO uses structured chosen/rejected records and requires an
authenticated frozen reference. Reward mode trains a masked last-token scalar
head with pairwise BCE. PPO performs online rollouts with authenticated frozen
reference/reward checkpoints, per-token log-probabilities, KL, GAE, and clipped
minibatch epochs. `--adapter none|lora|qlora` selects full update, dense-base
LoRA, or a frozen deterministic NF4 group-64 base.

`--kquant-profile k-quant-17gb|k-quant-dynamic` selects immutable official
GGUF-base LoRA for SFT/DPO; it is not NF4 QLoRA. The main digest and tensor
table are pinned in adapter state, DPO reference must be the identical packed
base, and only adapters are saved. Packed reward/PPO is rejected.

Full-BF16 AR/SFT accepts `--pipeline-parallel-size N` and
`--pipeline-cuda-devices d0,...,dN-1`. Without an explicit rank the CLI starts
one process per distinct device, assigns contiguous layer stages, and shares a
temporary NCCL unique-ID file. Use `--nccl-lib`, optionally
`--distributed-timeout-seconds`/`--distributed-reserve-bytes`, or
`--print-distributed-plan` for admission planning. Rank-local checkpoints bind
the world/stage layout and cannot resume under a different layout.

`nfn train --runtime native-cuda --graph-file GRAPH ...` runs the same
source-safe compatibility pass before binary resolution. Thirteen exact reviewed
profiles report `execution_ready: true`: `gpt2`, `gpt2_megakernel`,
`gpt2_moa`, `gpt2_qknorm`, `gpt2_softcap`, `gpt2_stable`, `gpt2_zloss`,
canonical `llama`, `llama_fast`, and standard-MoE `moe`, `mixllama`, and
`mixllama_fast`, plus proof-bound `gpt2_diff` training. The other 53 shipped profiles fail closed with stable
node-specific JSON and never route through a diagnostic transition sampler.
`gpt2_diff` is training-ready only after the trusted planner emits
`native-training-proof.json`, and it remains not graph-planned
migration/resident execution-ready. The trainer requires the exact
graph/fingerprint/proof triplet before plan/Tile/CUDA work; the unkeyed proof
digest is local-handoff integrity, not caller authenticity. Its low-level compiled trainer learns one
FP32 lambda per layer and writes a source-bound, DONE-gated five-binary bundle
plus `model_XXXXXXXX.diff.json`. The metadata schema is
`neuralfn.native_gpt2_diff.training_checkpoint` version 2; its unchanged binary
formats retain `checkpoint_kind=trained_dense_v5_plus_diff_v1`. Continuation
requires the planner-issued graph, verified lowercase fingerprint, and proof.
Preflight completes before Tile/CUDA/H2D and binds graph and artifact identity,
optimizer/microbatch and sampler counters, seed explicitness/value,
batch/accumulation shape, ordered training-shard contents, optimizer/LR and
absolute schedule horizon, LM-head chunk, effective BF16 routes, and a canonical
numerics profile of supported effective routes. Validation shards are excluded from the training
identity. Migration and resident inference do not consume the bundle yet, so
their capability matrix remains 12 ready and 55 blocked even though graph
training is 13 ready and 54 blocked.
The learned trainer requires its
learned-lambda ABI; the legacy fixed-lambda differential ABI remains outside
this path with rounded-output/non-layer-local backward correctness debt.
`nfn migrate graph-to-native` rejects `.pt`, raw `.bin`, and metadata-v2
`.diff.json` weights paired with this graph before generic checkpoint dispatch
or output creation. Keep the complete bundle until a differential inspector
and resident consumer are implemented.
Canonical LLaMA additionally requires exact RMSNorm/RoPE/MHA-or-GQA/dense-
attention/gate-first-SwiGLU, biasless, dropout-zero, untied topology. Its plan
owns layers, width, hidden rounding, heads, vocabulary, context, RoPE, and the
source SHA-256. The current executables remain selector-driven, so a ready plan reports
`trainer_consumes_native_ir: false` and `graph_preflight_enforced: true`. A
real run snapshots the validated graph and planning sidecars under
`OUTPUT_DIR/native-ir`, then passes that immutable graph plus canonical
selector/geometry to the trainer. LLaMA verifies graph byte identity before
dataset/CUDA initialization and at checkpoint write. `--dry-run`, plan/check
actions, and command printing cannot enter the dataset loop and do not
materialize those artifacts. Caller-selected train/smoke actions are rejected.

## Legacy inference migration guard

The retained graph-backed and graphless Parameter Golf paths are compatibility
routes. Ordinary calls still reach their existing runtime, but first print a
deprecation warning:

```bash
nfn infer --graph artifacts/model.json --weights artifacts/model.pt --prompt "Hello"
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts/final_model.pt --checkpoint-tokenizer tokenizer.model --prompt "Hello"
```

For `--graph`, the warning derives an adjacent `<graph-stem>-native` output and
prints the exact `nfn migrate graph-to-native` command with every supplied path
quoted safely for a shell. Graphless `--checkpoint MODEL.pt`, and
`--weights MODEL.pt` without `--graph`, cannot prove topology. Those warnings
state that a matching NeuralFn graph is required and print this deliberately
unresolved template rather than guessing a graph path:

```bash
nfn migrate graph-to-native \
  --graph MATCHING_GRAPH.json \
  --weights artifacts/final_model.pt \
  --output-dir artifacts/final_model-native
```

Legacy artifacts cannot opt into resident-only features. `--serve`,
`--kv-cache turboquant`, and `--kv-cache=turboquant` return exit code 2 before
the native server or full legacy runtime is entered, while also printing the
artifact-specific migration guidance. A migrated `.pt` is a validated generic
graph/tensor bundle, not a resident model. A separately compatible resident
native checkpoint is still required before serving or TurboQuant can be used.

## Interactive inference transcripts

Interactive TTY graph inference defaults to `--chat-mode transcript` and opens
the installed Rich native-chat TUI. Its banner shows the selected runtime,
weight precision, cache, speculation mode, renderer, context, and sampling;
assistant panels show new/reused prefill tokens, decode tok/s, and DFlash
acceptance. Use `--chat-mode stateless` or `/mode stateless` for independent
turns. An initial `--prompt` is the first transcript turn;
`--system-prompt TEXT` adds a retained leading instruction that remains active
in stateless mode and after `/reset`. `--chat-template
auto|plain_roles|PATH` prefers a usable artifact/tokenizer template, accepts a
data-only marker template from a file, and warns before falling back to
`plain_roles` in CLI sessions.

The interactive commands are `/mode stateless|transcript`, `/show` (alias
`/stats`), `/reset`, `/clear`, `/help`, and `/exit`. `/show` reads live
resident statistics without recreating the model. For packed Glimmer CUDA,
its `cuda_device_argmax_calls` and `cuda_device_argmax_rows` values prove that
ordinary greedy target selection or greedy DFlash proposal/verification
selection stayed on device. `/reset` clears transcript turns and resident
cache state but retains the configured system prompt. The default CLI
completion allowance is 512 tokens; pass `--max-new-tokens N` to change it.

Before encoding, the CLI reserves the requested output-token capacity. It
trims oldest complete conversation groups while retaining leading
developer/system messages and the newest user/tool request, and fails when
that mandatory remainder cannot fit. Configured role/EOS delimiters are
stripped from ordinary assistant text before it enters process-local history.
Muse Glimmer additionally uses an ATEM-aware response parser: private
`to=self` content is hidden and never retained, while only `to=user` content
is displayed and added to the next turn. A truncated private-only completion
fails closed with a suggestion to increase the token allowance. Non-TTY
inference remains one-shot, and the legacy raw native-checkpoint sampler
remains one-shot. Native Execution manifest artifacts instead load one
resident model/session and use the same transcript controls with exact-prefix
cache reuse. See
[Resident Native Artifact CLI Inference](native-cli-inference.md).

For canonical LLaMA, artifact-directory, manifest, and exact contained
`model.f32` invocations select the resident path. A non-interactive
`--prompt-tokens` request remains tokenizer-free; when no supported text codec
exists, the CLI warns once and prints generated token IDs as comma-separated
integers. Text prompts and interactive transcripts do not use that fallback.

The same manifest-first rule applies to graph-bound standard-MoE artifacts for
`moe`, `mixllama`, and `mixllama_fast`. Their exact contained `model.f32` uses
the real resident router/expert forward and lossless cache; it does not enter the
native-family transition sampler. Raw token IDs remain tokenizer-free, while
text and HTTP use still require compatible tokenizer/chat metadata. Explicit
TurboQuant fails closed.

## Native text embeddings

`nfn train --base-model embedding` opens model-aware embedding setup rather
than LM setup. It accepts `--embedding-stage
pretrain|posttrain|finetune|resume`, `--embedding-architecture
bert|gpt-derived`, pooling/vector dimensions, record batch sizes, raw-text MLM
and contrastive weights, triplet margin, and `--adapter-type none|lora|qlora`.
Supply either a JSON dataset array with `--embedding-datasets-manifest PATH` or
repeat `--embedding-dataset PATH` for raw-text sources.

```bash
nfn train --base-model embedding \
  --embedding-datasets-manifest datasets.json \
  --embedding-stage pretrain \
  --embedding-dim 384 \
  --output-dir artifacts/embed-384

nfn embed --checkpoint artifacts/embed-384/embedding_model.bin \
  --text "example text"
```

From-scratch runs configure `--hidden-dim`, `--num-layers`, `--num-heads`, and
`--intermediate-dim`. To import an existing transformer, use
`--embedding-hf-model MODEL_ID_OR_PATH` and optionally
`--embedding-hf-revision REVISION`; the importer accepts BERT-family and
GPT-2-family safetensors or plain PyTorch ZIP state-dict layouts, discovers wrapper prefixes by tensor suffix,
copies tokenizer assets, and overrides the native geometry while preserving
the activation and LayerNorm epsilon. It never loads Torch. Install
`neuralfn[embeddings]` for Hub downloads and tokenizer.json
support; local BERT `vocab.txt` WordPiece import uses the standard library.

Warm-start post-training/fine-tuning uses `--base-checkpoint`; it imports model
weights but resets optimizer state. Exact continuation uses
`--embedding-stage resume --resume-from-checkpoint DIR` and requires the paired
`embedding_optimizer.bin`. Adapter selections freeze the base tensors and train
LoRA matrices on every attention/MLP linear and the final projection; QLoRA
reads all of those frozen linear weights through NF4 group-64 dequantization.
Both resumable adapter and merged checkpoints are written.
`NFNEMB1` compact checkpoints are not loadable by this transformer path; create
a new `NFNEMB2` base or import a supported HF model.
The legacy dense-GPT `--train-embedding-lm` flag remains a next-token
token-table diagnostic and is not used by this model type.

## Install

```bash
cd cli
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ..
pip install -e .
nfn --help
```

The first editable install exposes the `neuralfn` and `server` packages from
the repo root. The second installs the CLI entrypoint declared by
`cli/pyproject.toml`.

The default SDK install is the lean native/core surface. Root `nfn --help` /
no-argument startup, `nfn train|infer|eval --help`, `nfn kernels ... --help`,
`nfn kernels list [--json]`, CUDA Tile registry metadata, and native GPT
training work without installing or importing Torch, NumPy, tokenizers,
HuggingFace datasets, graph-analysis packages, or server dependencies. Install
`pip install -e ".[tile-cuda]"` for Torch-free native CUDA Tile build tooling,
`pip install -e ".[datasets]"` for raw-text tokenization and HF dataset cache
materialization, `pip install -e ".[graph]"` for Python graph helpers,
`pip install -e ".[server]"` for the FastAPI/editor/MCP backend. The root
`.[all]` extra is also Torch-free, and NeuralFn no longer exposes a `.[torch]`
extra. Legacy graph-backed Torch code requires a separately managed PyTorch
install outside NeuralFn's package metadata. The no-Torch verifier requires
`requirements.txt` to stay dependency-empty and checks `requirements-full.txt`
only for Torch-family packages, so optional server/dataset helpers cannot
become default native-training dependencies.
Importing `nfn_impl` for parser/planner helpers also keeps Torch, NumPy,
`server.dataset_manager`, graph ops, parameter-golf Torch helpers, and
`train_jepa_semantic` lazy until a command path actually needs the graph-backed
runtime.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `nfn train` | Configure and launch native training, or run a composed recipe through explicit legacy SDK APIs. |
| `nfn infer` | Load an exported graph or supported graphless checkpoint and generate text from a prompt. |
| `nfn eval` | Run validation batches and prompt probes, then write a JSON report. |
| `nfn kernels` | Inspect CUDA Tile kernel coverage and local CUDA Tile diagnostics. |

On an interactive terminal, bare `nfn train` opens the native training TUI.
Use `nfn train --tui` to force it, or `nfn train --no-tui ...` when you want a
scripted native default run. The TTY interface opens as a Rich dashboard that
matches the colorful panel style of the `nfn infer` chat screen after model
selection. Model, template, dataset, output, logs, and every native-training
hyperparameter are visible on one screen in an editable grid with current value
and default columns. Move with Up/Down, press Enter to edit only the selected
row, press `r` to run, or press `p` to print the resolved native command without
launching. The first hyperparameter row is `Steps`, defaulting to `20000`,
followed by sequence length, batch sizing, learning rate, LR schedule, final LR
fraction, weight decay, warmup, eval cadence, eval batches, loss cadence, and
progress cadence. GPT-family
template edits use the same full catalog shown by
`nfn-native-train --base-model gpt --list-templates`, with the shipped Python
catalog as a fallback when the native binary is not available. Evo-capable
templates such as `dense-jepa-evo-modern` add evo layer/cadence/population/
mutation/tournament/elite rows, and model or template edits refresh the grid immediately. TUI
launches label setup/train/eval output in a structured training panel. Native
family entries such as dense JEPA route through their compiled family trainer and
are expected to perform optimizer-updated training rather than silently
substituting diagnostic smoke loops. Non-TTY `--tui`
keeps the deterministic prompt fallback for tests and automation. The
wrapper-level `--train-log-file PATH` and `--eval-log-file PATH` options work
outside the TUI too; train logs capture native progress stderr, and eval logs
capture validation lines plus the final stdout JSON payload.
Compiled native-family trainers also accept `--native-checkpoint PATH` and the
common `--checkpoint PATH` alias. With `--print-plan`, PATH may be a checkpoint
directory, an emitted native-family model JSON, or the `.f32` parameter sidecar
itself; the C++ preflight resolves the parameter sidecar, validates its byte
size against the current family/template parameter layout, streams the float32
state, and reports the result in the `native_checkpoint` JSON object. This is a
resume-read preflight only until the production family parameter store loads the
sidecar into device parameters before the training loop.
`--print-plan` also reports a `production_state_contract` object for these
family binaries. It names the shared `FamilyDeviceParameterStore`,
`FamilyOptimizerState`, and `FamilyProductionStep` boundary, reports resolved
parameter-buffer count plus element/byte totals, confirms deterministic init and
full-sidecar support, and shows whether the binary was compiled with
`NFN_NATIVE_PRODUCTION_LOOP=1` and whether the full-geometry status gate is
enabled. It also reports named production parameter-role
counts for the base transformer, MoE, JEPA, semantic, seq2seq, diffusion, TTT,
universal, HNet, and Jamba subsystems. The same contract reports the selected
family production-step descriptor, including required roles and planned
full-geometry forward/backward stages; default diagnostic binaries report
`full_geometry_forward_backward: true` and report their family-specific
`persistent_tile_*_full_geometry_forward_backward` implementation by default.
Both native gates are enabled for every target emitted by
`tools/build_native_missing_trainers.sh`. Production-macro builds run the
token embedding and LM-head objective through Tile-ABI forward/backward kernels
and report
`production_step_tile_lm_row_count` for the real device rows. That bridge reads the live `token_embedding.weight`
and full-geometry LLaMA blocks apply the live RMSNorm affine weights through
`nfn_native_tile_vector_binary_float32`, including norm-weight gradients before
the persistent AdamW update. Full and specialty paths process LM-head logits in
bounded 128-row chunks and accumulate their CE, hidden-state, and LM-head
weight gradients. Their attention geometry follows separate Q/K/V
projections with configurable query/KV heads; use `--num-heads N`,
`--num-kv-heads N`, and `--rope-theta N` (defaults `4`, `2`, and `10000`).
Preset names for Gemma-3, long-context LLaMA/Qwen, and DeepSeek-V4 also select
their configured sparse window, sink, block, and compression-stride arguments
in plan metadata and both attention directions.
The full-geometry LLaMA binary also applies native quantized linear deltas for
`ternary_b158`, `fp8_llama`, `deepseek_v4`, and `mxfp4_llama`. Forward and
linear-input backward use per-row ternary, FP8 E4M3, or MXFP4 E2M1 block-32
values selected by the template; float32 straight-through weight gradients
continue through the persistent AdamW state. Plan JSON reports the selected
contract in `architecture.linear_quantization`.
For canonical 86-d semantic-family runs, the native production step now includes
the template-shaped `semantic_projector.topic_heads.weight` per-term topic-head
buffer. Token-shard semantic batches can derive the full target matrix on
device, run packed per-term semantic alignment loss/backward, consume packed
per-term target-topic teachers for route distillation, and update the per-term
head through persistent AdamW. The legacy compact 86-wide topic head remains for
noncanonical fallback runs, but canonical mode no longer forwards or
backpropagates through it. Plan and runtime JSON report
`full_family_semantic_chunk_projector_per_term_topic_head_parameter_layout`,
`full_family_semantic_chunk_projector_per_term_alignment_device_forward_backward`,
`full_family_semantic_target_topic_per_term_route_distillation_device_backward`,
`full_family_semantic_canonical_compact_topic_head_retired`, and
`full_family_semantic_target_matrix_device_token_derivation`. Semantic-router
JEPA also exposes the template-named `online_chunk_projector.*` and frozen
`target_chunk_projector.*` topic/signature/residual surfaces, while retaining
the route-time `semantic_projector.*` compatibility buffers; plan/runtime JSON
reports `full_family_semantic_chunk_projector_online_target_parameter_surface`.
The layout-smoke `parameter_layout.torch_state_dict_aliases` and checkpoint
`architecture_parameter_layout.torch_state_dict_aliases` arrays export the
packed native topic-head tensors as identical per-dimension Torch
`topic_heads.N.weight` aliases and report
`full_family_semantic_chunk_projector_modulelist_state_dict_aliases`.
The broader
`full_family_semantic_chunk_projector_per_term_topic_head_exact_parity` field
remains false while remaining semantic chunk projector/router gaps are closed.
When semantic shared experts are configured, `--print-plan` and runtime JSON
also report
`full_family_semantic_router_shared_experts_always_on_route_width` and
`full_family_semantic_shared_plus_topk_route_device_forward_backward`; the
native route tensor width is `semantic_shared_experts + top_k`, with shared
experts occupying the leading route slots.
Canonical per-term semantic-router plans also report
`full_family_semantic_router_forced_target_candidate_mask_device_forward`; that
means the native route selector restricts dynamic top-k candidates to valid
semantic target dimensions when a row has forced targets, matching the template
router's forced-mask behavior while leaving `route_logits` intact for auxiliary
losses.
The `qwen3_longctx` selector additionally applies YaRN RoPE interpolation in
the native full graph, defaulting to factor `4` and original context `2048`.
Use `--rope-factor N` and `--original-max-position N` to override those
values; plan JSON reports the resolved scaling fields. KV-PCA uses the
dedicated native encode/decode parameter layout described below.
The `diff_transformer` selector uses the native differential-attention branch:
split query/key head channels feed two causal attention calls, their outputs
are combined with the persisted learnable `attention.diff_lambda`, then
head-wise RMSNorm and the fixed `1 - lambda_init` scale are applied. Backward
collects the scalar lambda gradient into the persistent AdamW state. Plan JSON
reports `attention_variant="differential"` and `differential_lambda`.
Parameter sidecars created before this buffer existed must be regenerated.
The `kv_pca_llama` selector persists four shared per-head matrices per layer:
`kv_pca_encode.k.weight`, `kv_pca_encode.v.weight`,
`kv_pca_decode.k.weight`, and `kv_pca_decode.v.weight`. The native graph
compresses K/V after RoPE, decodes them before attention, and reverses both
linear stages during backward while collecting all matrix gradients into
AdamW. The default compressed width is `head_dim // 4`; plan JSON reports
`attention_variant="kv_pca"`, `kv_pca_enabled=true`, and
`kv_pca_compressed_dim`; inactive MLA fields report zero for this selector.
For standard-MoE `mixllama` and `deepseek-v4`, the same full-geometry build
also dispatches normalized hidden rows through live router top-k and expert
SwiGLU gate/up/down buffers, with router and expert gradients entering the
persistent optimizer state. Configured `layers_per_expert` stacks execute
sequential gate/up/down stages and accumulate route gradients across depth.
DeepSeek-V4 additionally uses separate Q/K/V projections, QK RMSNorm, native
sink/window/block/compression-stride sparse attention in both directions, and
mHC residual mixing. Its plan JSON reports
`attention_variant="native_sparse"`, `native_sparse_csa_attention_enabled=true`,
`mla_attention_enabled=false`, and zero inactive MLA dimensions. The shipped
DeepSeek-V4 static sink/window/block/stride CSA path reports
`full_family_deepseek_v4_native_sparse_csa_exact_parity: true`, while
`full_family_deepseek_v4_mla_template_required: false` and
`full_family_deepseek_v4_learned_csa_indexer_template_required: false` make the
inactive MLA and learned-indexer contracts explicit. Mixed FP8/MXFP4 native
storage is reported through `architecture.linear_quantization` and
`architecture.expert_quantization`. Its MoE router uses the template
`sqrt_softplus` scorer and reports
`architecture.router_score_fn="sqrt_softplus"`.
Enable both production and full-geometry target
selectors before relying on covered status. MoE-JEPA combines the routed graph
with live JEPA matrices. Its full objective pools masked sequence rows with
`latent_pool`, applies `latent_mse_loss` to the batch latents, and uses
device-side `latent_pool_backward` to broadcast both target and online latent
gradients back through the mask weights. The deterministic native mask values
are constructed on device; configure them with `--jepa-mask-ratio N` and
`--jepa-mask-strategy random|block`. Semantic-router combines the routed graph
with semantic projection CE when the template selects those buffers. Semantic-router full
layouts also persist hash-bucket embeddings, table-gate logits, and
per-dimension bias; the Tile semantic-hash indices feed route-logit gradients
back into those trainable buffers through a host reduction. The native semantic
JEPA path also projects target-encoder rows through the reduced semantic-vocab
projection and distills those target-topic logits into router gradients before
hash/table backward. Fresh semantic hash projection initialization now matches
the Torch/NumPy seeded hasher, while per-term topic-head and route-evolution
parity remain pending. Full semantic routing uses the
configured chunk-anchor broadcast and aggregates its route gradients back to
anchor rows. Full semantic rows also add the bounded smoothed-target route
distillation objective to the reduced router gradient.
DeepSeek-V4 additionally exposes live per-layer
`residual.beta_logit.weight` buffers and uses the Tile vector-binary mHC
residual mix in forward and reverse mode, including beta-logit gradients in
the persistent optimizer map. DeepSeek-V4 now uses FP8 E4M3 quantized-linear
dispatch for its native linear projections and MXFP4 E2M1 block-32 expert reads
for routed SwiGLU expert weights; its router uses sqrt-softplus selected-route

template uses the single-stream `ManifoldHyperConnectionStage`, and native

with `full_family_mhc_multi_stream_template_required: false`. Current plan JSON
separates active MLA, KV-PCA, native-sparse CSA, quantized-linear,
expert-quantization, single-stream-mHC, and router-score contracts with explicit
booleans and zeroed inactive dimensions; for `deepseek_v4`, the active
native-sparse CSA contract is exact and MLA plus a learned CSA indexer are
reported as not required by the preset.
DeepSeek-V4/Gemma QK-normalized presets also run the existing RMSNorm Tile
primitive over each Q/K head before RoPE and its reverse-mode counterpart
before Q/K projection gradients.
Dense `jepa` and `semantic-dense-jepa` targets additionally run live
target-encoder/projector/predictor matrices and merge latent-MSE gradients into
the AR transformer step when both production gates are enabled. MoE-JEPA and
semantic-router template names select the corresponding full objective branch.
The semantic-router full graph also consumes loop-derived semantic target rows
through `semantic_vocab_projection.weight` and merges semantic CE gradients;
its expert count must satisfy the configured shared-plus-vocab-plus-free

causal-chunk-state forward/backward path. Full-specialized `jamba`, `seq2seq`,

their native step is selected because it assumes the diagnostic global
`qkv`/MoE layout. Default binaries now report the covered full-family
contract; exact template-specific parity remains a separate audit item.

`auxfree_moe_jepa_evo` marks the production-step
descriptor with `auxfree_moe_balance` and skips the chained-block,
selected-route, and routed-combine sampled route-balance gradient terms, then
refreshes `router.auxfree_bias.weight` from sampled top-k route-load imbalance
outside AdamW before staging gradients through
`FamilyOptimizerState`, and
validates that every trainable parameter buffer has parameter-dependent sparse
gradient coverage, requiring at least one finite nonzero sparse gradient in
each trainable buffer range. The bridge rejects non-finite sparse gradients and
drops zero-valued entries before `FamilyOptimizerState` accumulation; the
shared optimizer entrypoint also rejects non-finite sparse scales, raw values,
scaled values, and accumulated values before device-buffer writes. Dataset
runtime JSON reports semantic target batch/row counters when loop-derived
semantic targets are supplied to the production step. Dataset
loops instantiate the selected descriptor
through `make_native_family_production_step(...)`, which returns the shared
`FamilyProductionStep` interface so concrete family implementations can replace
the bridge without changing every loop call. The C++ source has a production
bootstrap helper that maps `family_parameter_buffers()` into the shared store
specs, validates those role bindings against the live store, and allocates the
optimizer state when a real production loop calls it; default diagnostic loops report
`production_state_runtime.required: false` and leave it unused.
When a family binary is compiled with `NFN_NATIVE_PRODUCTION_LOOP=1`, the
dataset loop treats that bootstrap as mandatory and fails before the first
training step if resume resolution, CUDA runtime loading, deterministic
parameter initialization, or optimizer-state allocation cannot complete. Runtime
JSON also reports whether the live `FamilyDeviceParameterStore` checksum was
computed and the checksum value, giving resumed production loops observable
evidence that the sidecar reached device state before training.
Production-ready family checkpoints also use that bootstrap: the model writer
copies the live `FamilyDeviceParameterStore` to host and emits the complete
float32 parameter sidecar with `write_family_full_parameter_sidecar()`. Default
diagnostic binaries keep their sampled-update checkpoint path and continue to
report full-architecture optimizer persistence as missing.
Production-enabled binaries also move
`optimizer-updated-full-architecture-parameter-persistence` from
`native_training_missing_requirements` into
`native_training_completed_requirements` in plan/catalog payloads, matching the
required bootstrap and live sidecar path.
For production-enabled binaries, sampled LM, chained block-state, and dense FFN gradients now enter the shared
optimizer path before persistence through a concrete
`FamilyProductionStep::forward_backward(...)` bridge: it combines
parameter-dependent embedding/head, chained block-state, and dense SwiGLU FFN
gradients, validates that every trainable family parameter buffer has
parameter-dependent sparse gradients, sets sparse
global gradients in `FamilyOptimizerState`, runs its global-norm/many-tensor
AdamW step, then writes the updated live parameter store. The shared boundary
remains the common implementation point for exact preset-delta work.
LLaMA, dense JEPA, semantic dense JEPA, semantic-router MoE, the shared
standard-MoE/MoE-JEPA dataset loops, Jamba, seq2seq, diffusion, TTT,
universal, and HNet run that persistent sampled-LM plus chained block-state
and dense-FFN production step during
training microbatches when the binary is production enabled; their
`production_state_runtime.production_step_count`,
`production_optimizer_step_count`, and `production_step_gradient_count` show
the loop-time handoff and the one-AdamW-update-per-optimizer-step boundary,
`production_step_parameter_dependent_gradient_buffer_count` reports how many
trainable buffers received parameter-dependent sparse gradients, while
`production_step_persistent_parameter_buffer_count` reports how many live
parameter buffers the step validated through `FamilyDeviceParameterStore`
before optimizer gradients were written. `production_step_chained_block_layer_count`
and `production_step_chained_block_row_count` report the chained block-state
coverage executed by the bridge, and
`production_step_auxfree_bias_refresh_count` reports aux-free router-bias
refreshes when an aux-free buffer is present. Real full-geometry family backward
implementations now report covered status in the default full-family binaries;
controlled diagnostic builds can still exercise the sampled bridge explicitly.
When `NFN_NATIVE_FAMILY_PRODUCTION_STEP_CHECKSUM=1`, the runtime also copies
the live parameter store from the resident `FamilyDeviceParameterStore` after
each production-step call and recomputes
`production_step_parameter_store_checksum`.
`production_step_parameter_store_checksum_count` counts those post-step checks,
and `production_step_parameter_store_checksum_changed` is true when the latest
checksum differs from the initial or resumed store checksum. These fields prove
that the resident production store changed after AdamW or route-evo on the
default full-family path.
The exact `seq2seq` target runs its Tile-ABI composition by default; the
target/all environment variables remain controlled-build overrides. It runs encoder
self-attention, decoder causal self-attention, decoder-to-encoder
cross-attention, encoder and decoder SwiGLU FFNs, token CE, and reverse-mode
QKV/FFN/LM/embedding gradients. FFN gradients accumulate into the live
per-layer `ffn_gate_up.weight` and `ffn_down.weight` buffers. Packed QKV/shared
FFN parity remains a preset audit item.
The exact `ttt-llama` target runs its corresponding composition by default; it runs the live
base/down/tanh/up residual inner update, token CE, and reverse-mode TTT/LM/
embedding gradients through the surrounding TTT transformer and shared
optimizer. Use `--ttt-hidden-dim N` to keep
the native inner down/up buffers aligned with the template's configured TTT
width; the default is `32`.
The exact `diffusion` target is promoted in normal builds. Its Tile-ABI
composition applies deterministic timestep-driven masking, runs the full
transformer trunk, and backpropagates denoise-head CE into the denoiser and
token embedding; the graph has no timestep-embedding parameter.
The exact `seq2seq` target is also promoted in normal builds. Its persistent
Tile composition runs encoder self-attention, decoder causal and cross-
attention, stacked FFNs, token CE, and shared many-tensor AdamW.
The exact `ttt-llama` target is promoted as well; its inner base/down/tanh/up
update is composed with the full transformer backbone before shared AdamW.
The exact `universal-llama` target is promoted with tied recurrence and ACT
halting composed with the full transformer backbone before shared AdamW.
The exact `jamba` target is promoted with its Mamba state/head path composed
with the attention/MoE backbone before shared AdamW.
The exact `universal-llama` target runs its Tile-ABI recurrence by default; it runs the
configurable tied recurrence (`--max-recurrence-steps`, default `4`), ACT
remainder weights (`--halt-epsilon`, default `0.01`), Tile ACT weighted-sum,
halt-gate BCE, LM CE, and reverse-mode recurrent/halting/embedding gradients.
The universal transformer parameter contract and status gates are covered by
the default family binary.
The exact `hnet-lm` target has an opt-in full Tile-ABI byte-patch transformer
composition under `NFN_NATIVE_MISSING_FULL_GEOMETRY_TARGETS=hnet-lm`; it runs
byte-patch embedding, the hidden-backbone RMSNorm/QKV/RoPE/causal-attention/
SwiGLU stack, final norm, byte merge, byte CE, and reverse-mode
gradients for every HNet architecture buffer before shared many-tensor AdamW.
Native patch geometry follows `--byte-patch-size N` and
`--byte-patch-stride N` (defaults `4` and the patch size), including the
shorter patch sequence passed through merge. Full-macro HNet plans report
`native-trainer-covered`, `native-loop-covered`, and no missing requirements.
Seq2seq production runs also report
`production_step_sampled_seq2seq_cross_attention_row_count` for sampled
decoder-to-encoder cross-attention rows consumed by the persistent bridge.
Diffusion production runs report
`production_step_sampled_diffusion_masked_denoise_row_count` for sampled masked
denoise rows consumed by the persistent bridge.
TTT production runs report `production_step_sampled_ttt_inner_update_row_count`
for sampled base/down/tanh/up residual inner-update rows consumed by the bridge.
Universal production runs report
`production_step_sampled_universal_recurrent_step_row_count` for sampled tied
recurrent/halt-gated rows consumed by the bridge.
Jamba production runs also report
`production_step_sampled_jamba_mamba_state_row_count` for sampled recurrent
Mamba-state rows consumed by the persistent bridge. This is still sampled host
composition, not the final full Tile-ABI Jamba layer schedule.
Those family dataset loops also honor `--checkpoint-every-steps N`: after a
completed optimizer step divisible by `N`, they write an intermediate
native-family model checkpoint with a step-suffixed prefix while preserving the
final checkpoint path. Pass `--checkpoint-every-steps 0` to disable periodic
family checkpoints.
The shared native-family production header
`neuralfn/csrc/native_train/family_production_train.h` provides that future
device parameter-store boundary: `FamilyDeviceParameterStore` owns one CUDA
float32 allocation per family parameter buffer, supports deterministic
initialization callbacks, exposes named buffer lookup and typed device
parameter views, reads `.f32` sidecars into device memory, and copies parameters
back to host for checkpoint writing. The compiled family binaries include this
header today, but their diagnostic loops do not yet construct the store as the
live training state.
Native-family plan and layout JSON now resolve parameter-buffer sizes from the
CLI geometry controls: `--model-dim`, `--hidden-dim`, `--mlp-multiplier`,
`--multiple-of`, `--vocab-size`, and `--padded-vocab-size`, alongside the
existing layer, expert, semantic, and top-k fields. The padded vocabulary
controls parameter rows while `vocab_size` records the public tokenizer
vocabulary. When `--hidden-dim` is omitted, LLaMA-style families use the
template's `8/3` SwiGLU multiplier rounded up to `256`; GPT-style families
retain a `4x` width. Pass both controls explicitly for custom geometry.
The header also provides `FamilyOptimizerState`, the matching optimizer-state
boundary for production family loops. It allocates per-buffer gradients and
AdamW moment tensors, builds the registered-buffer descriptor arrays for
`nfn_native_tile_adamw_step_many_with_device_scale_float32`, allocates optional
bf16 shadow parameter storage, computes gradient sum-of-squares and clip scale
through the Tile global-norm helpers, and uses
`nfn_native_tile_adamw_step_many_with_device_scale_bf16_shadow_float32` when
available so the shadow is refreshed during the same optimizer launch. The same
state can capture and replay the CUDA graph for the device optimizer body when
`NFN_NATIVE_FAMILY_PRODUCTION_CUDA_GRAPH=1` or a production-loop build leaves
the default enabled; sparse CPU gradient staging remains outside the graph until
family forward/backward implementations are kernel-backed. Existing
diagnostic loops still need to replace sampled substeps with real
forward/backward calls that fill those gradient buffers.
Native family plan/runtime JSON reports
`full_step_cuda_graph_capture_ready`, `cuda_graph_capture_scope:
"retained_forward_backward_optimizer_step"`, and `full_step_cuda_graph_blockers`
for the retained forward/backward+optimizer production-step graph contract.
Current shipped native-family production builds report an empty blocker list and
`full_step_cuda_graph_capture_ready: true` once that graph path is selected.
A three-step runtime audit of LLaMA, MixLLaMA, MoE-JEPA, dense JEPA,
semantic-dense JEPA, semantic-router MoE, DeepSeek-V4, Jamba, seq2seq,
diffusion, TTT, HNet, and universal-transformer now verifies one retained
forward/backward graph capture followed by two replays for each family.
The captured optimizer replay now includes global-norm clip, many-tensor AdamW,
and trainable-gradient zeroing through `nfn_native_tile_fill_many_float32`; the
old host-to-device zero-copy path is not used for graph replay. Uncaptured
default-stream optimizer steps keep a chunked host zero-copy fallback if device
zeroing fails. Large semantic-family descriptor sets now split gradient zeroing
into 32-buffer fill-many chunks, so optimizer graph capture can include semantic
family zeroing instead of rejecting the descriptor count.
Temporary workspace leases now replay from a warmed fixed sequence without
mutating pool/active metadata during `forward_backward`, so they are no longer
reported as a full-step CUDA graph blocker. Loss reporting is reduced to one
post-backward scalar-vector readback and reports
`full_family_loss_reporting_post_backward_scalar_vector_readback: true`; the D2H
copy now runs wrapper-side after `forward_backward` and reports
`full_family_loss_reporting_readback_deferred_outside_full_step_capture: true`
plus `full_family_loss_reporting_readback_wrapper_side: true`. Production-stream
steps now keep clip/AdamW/zero-grad on the same stream after forward/backward,
reporting `production_step_optimizer_same_stream_after_forward_backward: true`
and `production_step_stream_elides_pre_optimizer_synchronization: true`.
Standard-family runtime steps can retain and replay a matching reporting-mode
forward/backward graph after the warmed capture. Plan/runtime JSON exposes
`full_step_forward_backward_launch_sequence_stream_ordered: true`,
family-specific `full_step_forward_backward_launch_sequence_capture_eligible`,
`full_step_forward_backward_graph_replay_ready: false`, and zero
`full_step_forward_backward_graph_capture_count`/`full_step_forward_backward_graph_replay_count`
counters on plan output. Runtime steps for standard LLaMA/MoE/JEPA families plus
the Jamba, seq2seq, TTT, universal, HNet, diffusion, and semantic-family
specialty paths now
capture, instantiate, launch, and retain one warmed forward/backward graph body
after temporary replay leases are available; later matching reporting-mode
steps for those eligible families can replay that retained graph and increment the same
runtime replay counter. The retained replay path refreshes the device
hyperparameter AdamW host buffer before launch. The blocker list remains
family-aware, and specialty host-control blockers have now been removed for all
families.
Native-family optimizers now prefer graph-friendly many-tensor AdamW Tile ABI
variants that read LR, beta, epsilon, and bias-correction values from a
persistent device hyperparameter buffer. The optimizer stream updates that
buffer before AdamW, avoiding stale scalar launch arguments when the full-step
graph is eventually retained. Optimizer-only CUDA graphs using that ABI refresh
the buffer before replay and avoid recapture for LR/beta/eps and
bias-correction changes; scalar-argument fallback graphs still recapture on the
full hyperparameter tuple.
When native-family CUDA graph support is enabled,
the production wrapper now requests a reusable nonblocking production stream,

before the wrapper-side scalar-vector reporting readback. Plan/runtime JSON

    `specialty_universal_device_gradient_accumulation: true`. Semantic-family

uses it for direct optimizer-gradient accumulation. Production helper

Runtime JSON also reports
`temporary_pool_buffer_count`, `temporary_active_buffer_count`,
`temporary_metadata_reserved_buffer_count`, and
`temporary_active_buffer_high_water_count` so a warmed workspace pool, reserved
metadata capacity, and zero active leases are visible at step boundaries.
`temporary_replay_lease_count` increments when a warmed run leases temporary
buffers from the recorded sequence without mutating pool/active metadata
vectors, and `temporary_replay_plan_buffer_count` reports that sequence length.
By default, warmed production steps only arm/disarm the recorded lease cursors
and skip per-lease size/free-order checks inside the hot path; replay readiness
validates the planned pointer/size sequence against the inactive pool, so
helpers that reuse buffers within one step can still replay even when plan
length exceeds active high-water. Set
`NFN_NATIVE_FAMILY_TEMPORARY_REPLAY_VALIDATE=1` to run strict diagnostic
begin/end replay validation around each step; strict mode records allocation and
free sequences separately so reuse-heavy helpers are validated against their real
free order.
Semantic-family production steps stage host-derived semantic matrices into
persistent device workspace inside the same production-step wrapper and use the
wrapper CUDA stream when one is supplied.
Runtime JSON also reports `production_step_parameter_store_checksum_enabled`;
when that toggle is false, or when a future full-step capture wrapper supplies a
non-null production stream, the post-step checksum readback is skipped instead
of forcing D2H traffic around graph replay.
The same header defines the production step interface used by that future
loop: `FamilyProductionStep::forward_backward(...)` accepts a
`FamilyProductionBatchView` and a context with the shared parameter store,
optimizer state, CUDA stream, optimizer step, and accumulation position, then
returns a `FamilyProductionStepResult` with family losses and gradient/update
counts. The current sampled-LM/FFN bridge uses `accumulation_step` /
`accumulation_steps` from `FamilyProductionStepContext` to accumulate sparse
gradients across microbatches and defer the AdamW step until the final
microbatch. Concrete family implementations are still required for MixLLaMA,
DeepSeek, MoE-JEPA, semantic-router MoE, dense/semantic JEPA, Jamba, seq2seq,
diffusion, TTT, HNet, and universal-transformer.
Production status is intentionally behind both
`NFN_NATIVE_PRODUCTION_LOOP=1` and
`NFN_NATIVE_FULL_GEOMETRY_FORWARD_BACKWARD=1`.
`tools/build_native_missing_trainers.sh` forwards the 8th `build_one`
argument into the production-state define and a 9th argument into the
full-geometry status define, both defaulting to `1`; default family binaries
therefore report covered full-family status. For controlled diagnostic builds,
set either gate to `0`; for explicit target selection, set
`NFN_NATIVE_MISSING_PRODUCTION_LOOP_TARGETS=model_or_binary,...` to opt in
selected models or binary names, or `NFN_NATIVE_MISSING_PRODUCTION_LOOP_ALL=1`
to opt in every missing-family target for that build invocation.
Production checkpoint writing has the matching shared helper:
`write_family_full_parameter_sidecar()` writes host-copied float32 parameters,
computes the native-family parameter checksum over every element, and returns
`FamilyFullParameterCheckpointInfo` with full trained-element coverage.
Controlled diagnostic family builds can emit sampled-update sidecars, while
default family dataset loops copy the live device parameter store to host and
write the full sidecar.

Every command accepts `--plan` for the older recipe questionnaire and
`--plan-auto` for recommended recipe defaults without prompting. Help output
supports `--help-style short`, `--help-style long`, and `--help-style verbose`.

## Recipe model

Recipes are composed from a small set of choices:

| Choice | Values |
|--------|--------|
| Base model | `gpt`, `gpt2`, `gpt3`, `llama`, `nanogpt` |
| Topology | `dense`, `moe`, `semantic_router` |
| Router mode | `standard`, `semantic` |
| Objective overlay | `--jepa` |
| Runtime | default or `--megakernel` |
| Training mode | `pretrain`, `sft`, `dpo`, `ppo`, `reward_model` |
| Adapter | `none`, `lora`, `qlora`, `randmap` |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[base model] --> B[topology]
    B --> C{MoE?}
    C -- no --> D[dense AR or AR+JEPA]
    C -- yes --> E[standard or semantic router]
    E --> F[optional JEPA]
    F --> G[ModelSpec]
    D --> G
    G --> H[NeuronGraph]
    H --> I[TorchTrainer]
    I --> J[weights + graph artifacts]
```

Examples:

```bash
nfn train
nfn train --tui
nfn train --no-tui --base-model gpt --tinystories --train-log-file ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt/train.log --eval-log-file ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt/eval.log
nfn train --plan
nfn train --base-model gpt --dataset tinystories --eval-every-steps 1000
nfn train --base-model gpt3 --dataset tinystories --native-cuda-print-command --native-cuda-dry-run
nfn train --base-model gpt --template-name deepseek_v4 --dataset tinystories --native-cuda-print-command --native-cuda-dry-run
nfn-native-train --base-model jamba --native-cuda-smoke-jamba-mamba-state-step --native-cuda-tile-ops-lib build/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so
nfn-native-train --base-model jamba --native-cuda-smoke-jamba-layer-schedule-step --native-cuda-tile-ops-lib build/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so
nfn-native-train --base-model hnet-lm --native-cuda-smoke-hnet-byte-lm-loop-step --native-cuda-tile-ops-lib build/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so
nfn-native-train --base-model universal-llama --native-cuda-smoke-universal-transformer-loop-step --native-cuda-tile-ops-lib build/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so
nfn infer --graph ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/llama_fast.json --prompt "Once upon a time"
nfn infer --checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt --prompt-tokens 50256 --max-new-tokens 64
nfn infer --checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/final_model.pt --checkpoint-tokenizer ~/Downloads/fineweb_8192_bpe_lossless_caps_caseops_v1_reserved.model
nfn eval --base-model gpt2 --dataset shakespeare
nfn kernels list --json
nfn kernels list --status host_only --kind module --json
nfn kernels doctor
nfn kernels bench --device auto --iterations 200
nfn kernels examples
```

The Python CLI and TUI resolve the selected template family and final executable
before applying trainer-specific defaults. For example, `--base-model gpt
--template-name deepseek_v4` (including the equivalent GPT-catalog TUI
selection) dispatches to `nfn_deepseek_v4_native_train`; it removes the
synthesized dense-only `--model-family` and `--train-transformer-lm` selectors
and does not append the dense-GPT handoff's backend, activation, sampling, or
optimizer-quality defaults. Generic schedule values selected in the TUI, and
other compatible explicitly supplied options, remain forwarded. Non-dense
family trainers use an explicit
`--tile-ops-lib /path/to/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so` when supplied, or
their normal `build/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so` default when omitted.
`--tile-ops-lib linked` is valid only when the final executable is the linked
dense-GPT trainer and is rejected for family trainers.

When the final resolved trainer remains dense GPT, the Python `nfn train`/TUI
route refuses stale in-tree trainer artifacts and automatically selects only
`build/nfn_gpt_native_train_linked`. It does not fall back to the generic or
dynamic compatibility frontend. The linked build emits
`build/nfn_gpt_native_train_linked.inputs.sha256`, covering the executable,
trainer/token/preset/Tile sources, Tile library, and build scripts. A missing
manifest/input, an untracked expected input, or a content-hash mismatch marks
the executable stale; timestamps are not used for route approval. An
interactive terminal lists the stale inputs and prompts:
`Force-recompile build/nfn_gpt_native_train_linked and continue? [y/N]`.
The accepted rebuild is:

```bash
NFN_NATIVE_GPT_FORCE_REBUILD=1 \
  bash tools/build_native_gpt_cli_linked.sh build/nfn_gpt_native_train_linked
```

Non-interactive runs fail with that command instead of waiting for input.
`NFN_NATIVE_GPT_AUTO_REBUILD=1` accepts it automatically. Dense-GPT
`nfn train` ignores `NFN_NATIVE_TRAIN_CLI`, `NFN_NATIVE_GPT_CLI`, and
`NFN_NATIVE_GPT2_CLI`, so inherited environment cannot redirect the route.
Lower-level SDK and compatibility entrypoints retain their override contracts.
TUI launches display and append SHA-256 provenance for the selected executable
and Tile-ops library to the configured train log.

The training TUI is metric-transparent. Native progress lines are formatted as
readable labeled segments while preserving every emitted field, including
tokens, native elapsed time, tokens/second, sampled train loss, optimizer step,
microbatch geometry and completion counts, accumulation, effective batch size,
and eval/loss-due flags. Validation and setup fields are preserved the same
way. At completion, the concise result card is followed by a complete
human-readable metric view: nested result fields become dotted paths such as
`timing.train_tokens_per_second`, `train_losses[0].loss_mean`, and
`kernel_routes.attention_forward_scalar_launch_count`. This exposes all scalar,
list, and nested metrics without printing a raw JSON blob. Train/eval logs
continue to retain the original unformatted trainer streams.

## Kernel diagnostics

`nfn train --help`, `nfn infer --help`, `nfn eval --help`, and `nfn kernels ... --help` use lightweight static help from `cli/nfn.py` so basic CLI orientation does not import `nfn_impl`, Torch, or graph-backed runtime modules. `nfn kernels list` prints CUDA Tile registry coverage from builtin and optimizer metadata on the same lightweight path. Pass `--status tile|torch_fallback|host_only|delegated|planned` and/or `--kind function|module|optimizer|runtime` to filter the emitted specs while keeping the global coverage totals intact; JSON output includes `filters`, `filtered_spec_count`, and `unfiltered_spec_count`. JSON output includes `by_dtype` aggregate counts plus each spec's legacy `dtypes` tuple and `dtype_support` matrix for `float32`, `float16`, `float8_e4m3fn`, `float8_e5m2`, and `nvfp4`, with either `"supported"` or the reason that dtype is not yet advertised. Unsupported lower-precision entries use category-specific reasons for losses/reductions, optimizers, stochastic masks, integer/hash/routing outputs, source nodes, and delegated graph calls. The fp8-supported entries include scalar/simple elementwise kernels, direct and composite projections, and attention Q/K/V modules that dequantize activations to float32 and return float32 outputs where required. The NVFP4-supported entries currently cover packed projection-family activations for `linear`, LM/router/value/reward/denoise heads, tied LM head, KV PCA encode/decode, JEPA heads, deterministic LoRA/TTT/adapter projections, `bitlinear_ternary`, `fp8_linear`, `mx_linear`, MLP projections, and ACT halt projection, plus attention Q/K/V and shared attention inputs for SDPA, sparse attention variants, differential attention, causal/fused causal attention, MLA, and routed attention experts. `nfn kernels doctor` also reports the local `nvcc`, CUDA Tile header, `torch.cuda`, and compute-capability status. `nfn kernels bench` compares the old graph-walk helper, the static compiled PyTorch plan, and the Tile-requested compiled plan on a small scalar graph. `nfn kernels examples` lists checked-in examples and `nfn kernels examples --write --output-dir examples/tile_cuda` regenerates the per-registry SDK snippets. These commands accept `--json` for automation.

SM120 same-script native GPT benchmarks keep long-run warmup and measured-step
floors when those values are left unset, but explicit `NFN_SM120_NATIVE_WARMUP`,
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_CANDIDATE_WARMUP`, `NFN_SM120_NATIVE_STEPS`, and
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_CANDIDATE_STEPS` values are honored for bounded repro probes.

`nfn train`, `nfn infer`, and `nfn eval` accept and advertise
`--kernel-backend tile-cuda` only. Default CLI training commands dispatch to
compiled CUDA Tile C++ trainers or fail before graph-backed runtime imports;
`auto` and `torch` are not supported CLI training backends. `tile-cuda` requests
the implemented CUDA Tile fast path, build-loads the optional extension when
needed, and defaults to strict kernel enforcement so unsupported graph nodes or
tensor contracts fail instead of silently dropping to slower fallback paths.
Pass `--no-tile-cuda-strict` only when intentionally debugging compatibility
behavior. The registry currently accounts for all 138
training-relevant entries with 129 Tile-covered kernels/compositions, 7
host-only entries, and 2 delegated graph calls. `NFN_TILE_CUDA_BUILD=1` enables
extension builds for explicit Tile extension probes, and `NFN_TILE_CUDA_ARCH`
can override the architecture flag passed to `nvcc`. Install
`pip install -e ".[tile-cuda]"` if the active environment does not already
provide `ninja` for native CUDA Tile builds. NeuralFn no longer exposes a
`.[torch]` extra; graph-backed PyTorch execution requires a separately managed
PyTorch install outside the default CLI training workflow.

The native GPT compiled CLI has its own backend selector:
`--backend tile-cuda` (or Python wrapper `--kernel-backend tile-cuda`). `tile-cuda` is the default and only NeuralFn-owned compiled trainer for dense GPT. Use the parity benchmark script, not a training backend, for llm.kittens reference timing.
Graph-backed compatibility script guards that target the shared dense GPT
trainer now prefer the canonical `build/nfn_gpt_native_train` binary when no
`NFN_NATIVE_GPT_CLI` override is set. That default binary is built with the Tile
ops library as a direct dependency and self-selects `--tile-ops-lib linked`, so
direct default invocations avoid the dynamic Tile ops loader. Guards append
`--tile-ops-lib linked` unless the caller already supplied a Tile ops library
flag, so direct scripts such as `python cli/scripts/train_nanogpt.py ...` enter
the linked CUDA Tile trainer path instead of paying the dynamic Tile ops load.
This sentinel injection happens only after the final executable is known to be
the linked dense-GPT trainer; it is never inherited by a routed family binary.
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_CANDIDATE_PROFILE=lm_head_prob_only_combined_corrections`
compares the default LM-head route against the diagnostic probability-only
CE+dlogits path with combined target correction. That path uses vec8 normal
stores for aligned BF16 dlogits, but it remains default-off because the current
same-script RTX 5090 gate still regresses total train-loop and block-backward
timing. Runtime JSON reports prob-only samples with
`lm_head_ce_kernel_strategy:
no-loss-prob-only-dlogits-vec8-loads-normal-vec8-stores-plus-combined-target-correction`
and `lm_head_ce_bf16_vector_io_strategy:
vec8-loads-normal-vec8-stores`.
Jamba native coverage includes the compiled
`--native-cuda-smoke-jamba-mamba-state-step` preflight. It dispatches through
`nfn_jamba_native_train`, exercises causal chunk-state forward/backward,
projection head loss/backward, and AdamW via raw CUDA Tile ABI symbols, and
reports no Torch requirement or graph-editor tensor flow. The related
`--native-cuda-smoke-jamba-layer-schedule-step` action verifies the scheduled
Mamba-state/head/loss/backward/AdamW dispatch. Bare Jamba training now enters
the native token-shard dataset loop and reports `native-trainer-covered`,
`native-loop-covered`, and
`optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true` by default.
HNet native coverage exposes `--native-cuda-smoke-hnet-byte-lm-loop-step` for
the byte-patch embed/merge, head loss/backward, byte-patch backward smoke, and
AdamW schedule. It stays on compiled CUDA Tile binaries and keeps
`graph_editor_tensor_flow: false`.
The persistent family bridge also reports
`production_step_sampled_hnet_byte_patch_row_count` for sampled real-byte
embed-to-merge rows; the default HNet binary now uses the full hierarchical
Tile-ABI production loop.
Universal transformer coverage exposes
`--native-cuda-smoke-universal-transformer-loop-step` for the recurrent
linear/MSE/AdamW and ACT halt/weighted-sum/AdamW schedule, again without
graph-editor tensor flow.
The related rejected profile
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_CANDIDATE_PROFILE=lm_head_prob_only_combined_corrections_threads_512`
keeps the forced 256-versus-512 target-correction thread-count comparison
available. The CUDA 13.3 RTX 5090 3-step, 1-sample recheck improved the
non-cooperative diagnostic train-loop wall ratio to `0.993286x` and LM-head
backward to `0.986391x`, but failed the strict gate because steady-state
CUDA-event step time regressed to `1.001297x` and the candidate still trailed
llm.kittens at `1.039342x` train-loop wall time.
Native linear-backward kernel candidates should be isolated before full parity
runs with `bash tools/bench_linear_backward_candidate.sh`. The wrapper builds
`build/linear_backward_bench`, loads the raw Tile C ABI, and compares baseline
versus candidate symbols for strided BF16 dInput or dWeight kernels using
CUDA-event timing in one process. Select trainer-shaped profiles with
`NFN_LINEAR_BACKWARD_PROFILE=mlp-proj-dinput`, `mlp-proj-dweight`,
`mlp-fc-dinput`, `mlp-fc-dweight`, `qkv-dinput`, `qkv-dweight`,
`attn-proj-dinput`, `attn-proj-dweight`, `lm-head-dinput`, or
`lm-head-dweight`; `lm-head-dinput-cublaslt` and `lm-head-dweight-cublaslt`
exercise explicit forced-cuBLASLt diagnostic symbols for the padded-vocab
LM-head shapes. The CUDA 13.3 RTX 5090 isolated benchmark rejected those
cuBLASLt candidates at `1.017720x` dInput and `1.000576x` dWeight, so they stay
off the default trainer path. Set `NFN_LINEAR_BACKWARD_CANDIDATE_SYMBOL` for a
new C ABI symbol and `NFN_LINEAR_BACKWARD_MAX_RATIO=1.000` for a no-regression
gate. Keep the default `NFN_LINEAR_BACKWARD_WARMUP=1` or higher for candidate
comparisons so first-call cuBLAS/TK setup is not counted as kernel time.
The compiled runtime reports token-weight startup routes with
`token_weight_init_strategy`, `token_weight_vector4_strided_init_requested`,
`token_weight_padded_init_fusion_requested`,
`token_weight_padded_init_fusion_available`,
`token_weight_padded_init_fusion_enabled`, and
`token_weight_padding_zero_launches_elided`. On the default initializer path,
known-zero BF16 padding rows are zeroed in the same fused padded-vocab
initializer launch; JSON reports `token_weight_bf16_padding_memset_count` as
`0` on that default route. Set
`NFN_NATIVE_GPT_FUSE_TOKEN_WEIGHT_PADDED_INIT=0` only for paired startup
bisection against the older separate padding-zero/default vector4 path after
rebuilding the trainer-facing Tile ops library. The padded kernel writes
public-vocab BF16 shadow rows from the same conversion-based vector4 path as the
default initializer and still zeros padded rows in the same launch. The CUDA
13.3.33 dedicated RTX 5090 current llm.kittens parity rerun promoted it with
median train-loop `0.998418x`, median steady-state CUDA-event `0.998668x`, and
median tokens/sec `1.001805x`. The
`token_weight_vector4_strided` paired profile forces baseline
`NFN_NATIVE_GPT_TOKEN_WEIGHT_VECTOR4_STRIDED_INIT=0` versus candidate `=1`, so
the benchmark JSON has a visible strategy-value route change for the hidden
Tile dispatch.
Use `--base-model gpt` as the canonical native trainer surface. `gpt2` and
`gpt3` are dense GPT selector aliases that preserve their selected
`--model-family` labels when the compiled C++ frontend runs; GPT3 defaults to
a 2048-token context when selected through `--base-model gpt3` or
`--template-name gpt3`, unless a custom graph or explicit `--train-seq-len` is
supplied. The implicit GPT3 batch size is 32, preserving the default
65,536-token microbatch unless `--batch-size` is explicit.
`nfn-native-train --list-models --json` reports dense GPT coverage with
capability-specific fields: `transformer_lm_status`, `token_lm_status`, and
`geometry_status`. `gpt`, `gpt2`, `gpt3`, and `nanogpt` are implemented aliases
of the same native transformer trainer and all report
`geometry_status: "dense-gpt-template-geometry"` because the selected template
or custom graph, not the family label, chooses the effective architecture.
NanoGPT full-transformer training adds `--template-name nanogpt` and uses the
selected 320-wide/5-head/5-layer dense GPT geometry; explicit `--train-token-lm`
remains implemented for token-LM diagnostics. This is command dispatch and
geometry selection, not graph-faithful NanoGPT persistence/forward/residency:
the authored bias-free/dropout contract remains blocked against biased,
dropout-free dense-v5.
Plan and runtime JSON include `architecture_source`,
`architecture_contract`, `model_family_context_policy`, and
`resolved_native_template_name` so a run makes clear that the graph/template,
not the family label, chooses the architecture. The default public template is
`gpt`; today it resolves to the implemented dense GPT native topology.
`--native-cuda-print-plan` and `--native-cuda-check-tile-ops` still print the
raw Tile ABI plan or check the trainer-facing library. The Tile plan includes
the GPT-2 parameter layout and forward/backward/optimizer stage sequence that
the native loop executes.
`--native-cuda-smoke-tile-ops` / `--smoke-tile-ops` goes one step beyond
symbol checks: it loads `libnfn_native_train_tile_ops.so`, loads CUDA runtime,
launches `nfn_native_tile_fill_float32` on a tiny device buffer, copies the
result back, and reports JSON without Python, Torch, or graph-node payloads.
`--native-cuda-smoke-optimizer-step` / `--smoke-optimizer-step` allocates the
GPT-2 contiguous parameter, gradient, and AdamW moment buffers, runs one AdamW
call per registered GPT-2 parameter buffer with the correct decay/no-decay
setting, samples copyback values, and reports JSON.
`--native-cuda-smoke-lm-step` / `--smoke-lm-step` runs a tiny GPT-2-shaped
tied embedding/LM-head step through token embedding, linear logits, full-vocab
CE partials and workspace CE backward, linear input/weight backward, token
embedding weight backward, and AdamW.
`--check-tile-ops`, `--smoke-tile-ops`, `--smoke-optimizer-step`,
`--smoke-lm-step`, `--smoke-attention-step`, `--smoke-mlp-step`,
`--smoke-norm-residual-step`, and `--smoke-transformer-block-step` are no-data
preflight actions: the compiled CLI runs them before token-shard resolution, so
they do not require cached `fineweb_train_*.bin` shards and report
`token_shards_resolved: false` when no dataset was opened. Dataset-backed
smokes such as `--smoke-embedding-lm-step`, `--smoke-transformer-lm-step`, and
real training modes still resolve cached train/validation shards before running.
`--native-cuda-smoke-attention-step` / `--smoke-attention-step` runs a tiny
GPT-2 model-dim attention stage through qkv projection, QKV split, SDPA
forward/backward, QKV gradient merge, projection backward, and AdamW.
`--native-cuda-smoke-mlp-step` / `--smoke-mlp-step` runs a tiny GPT-2 MLP
stage through c_fc projection, GELU forward/backward, c_proj projection
backward, and AdamW.
`--native-cuda-smoke-norm-residual-step` / `--smoke-norm-residual-step` runs
GPT-2 LayerNorm, scaled residual add, LayerNorm affine/input backward, gradient
accumulation, and AdamW through raw Tile kernels.
`--native-cuda-smoke-embedding-lm-step` / `--smoke-embedding-lm-step` samples
a tiny cached uint16 token batch in C++ and runs token embedding, absolute
position embedding, embedding residual add, final LayerNorm, tied LM head, CE
backward, embedding/norm backward, and AdamW without graph-editor payloads.
`--train-embedding-lm` runs that GPT-2
embedding/final-norm/LM path as a real multi-step compiled loop over cached
train shards, with validation losses from validation shards controlled by
`--eval-every-steps`, `--eval-batches`, and `--eval-batch-size`.
`--native-cuda-smoke-transformer-block-step` /
`--smoke-transformer-block-step` composes GPT-2 LayerNorm, fused QKV attention,
real 12-head reshape/merge layout (`12 x 64`), residual adds, MLP, backward
passes, gradient accumulation, projection bias gradients, and AdamW updates for
all 12 GPT-2 block parameter buffers through raw Tile kernels.
`--native-cuda-smoke-transformer-lm-step` /
`--smoke-transformer-lm-step` samples cached uint16 tokens and runs
range-checked GPT-2 token IDs through token/position embeddings, one tiny
transformer block, final LayerNorm, tied LM head, CE forward/backward,
transformer backward, embedding backward, and AdamW for 16 parameter buffers
through raw Tile kernels.
`--train-transformer-lm` is the default strict compiled training action for that
transformer-LM path. It runs a full-vocab real-dim 12-layer multi-step loop
over cached shards with periodic validation records in `validation.losses`,
using the token/position embedding, transformer, final norm, tied LM head, CE
backward, a row-chunked tied LM-head/CE workspace, device-side global norm
gradient clipping, scratch-recompute activation tape, and 148-buffer AdamW raw
Tile kernels without Python/Torch.
Native JSON normally prints to stdout. Add `--json-out PATH` to the compiled
trainer to write that JSON directly to a file, or use the aliases
`--profile-json PATH` / `--stage-profile-json PATH` when collecting profiler
runs such as `NFN_NATIVE_GPT_STAGE_TIMING=1 build/nfn_gpt_native_train ...
--profile-json /tmp/nfn_profile.json`.
When the paired SM120 parity/candidate wrappers run with native stage timing,
their hot-stage text summary prints each selected `*.total_ms` metric with
sibling `count_mean` and `avg_ms_mean` values when present in the profile JSON.
This keeps candidate-vs-current gates readable in the terminal: per-layer block
regressions, LM-head chunk regressions, and one-time setup work can be
distinguished without opening the sidecar JSON.
The SM120 candidate wrapper also includes
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_CANDIDATE_PROFILE=lm_head_bf16_hidden_from_final_norm`, which
forces baseline separate LM-head BF16 hidden prepack and candidate final
LayerNorm BF16 hidden output. It is rejected for real runs unless
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_ALLOW_REJECTED_CANDIDATE_PROFILE=1` is set; the CUDA 13.3
RTX 5090 gate proved the strategy changed but regressed whole-loop wall time.
Profile JSON includes ranked arena request details in
`float_arena_request_stats.top_requests` and
`uint16_arena_request_stats.top_requests`. Each entry reports the suballocation
name, elements, bytes, and arena offset, so startup work can pair
`timing.setup_timing` with the actual buffers behind the large float and BF16
arena `cudaMalloc` calls. The same objects also include `family_count`,
`top_families`, `top_family_elements`, and `top_family_bytes`; repeated
per-block names are normalized as `block.*...` so layer-wide allocation
families can be compared across candidate runs. Dense GPT native JSON also
emits root allocation-pressure counters: `float_arena_allocated_bytes`,
`uint16_arena_allocated_bytes`, `transformer_arena_allocated_bytes`,
`activation_storage_bytes`, and `lm_head_bf16_logit_bytes`.
`tools/paired_kernel_speed.py` flattens those fields into native metric
summaries, so startup and storage candidates can be ratio-gated by memory
footprint as well as wall-clock timing.
The paired report also emits `train_sm120_recompute_contract`, which compares
baseline and candidate native runs against the llm.kittens `train-sm120.sh`
`-r 0` no-recompute reference. It records whether the native side is using a
full activation tape with zero backward recompute blocks or the current
scratch-recompute policy, and keeps no-recompute/full-tape promotion tied to
same-script candidate, baseline, and llm.kittens timing gates.
Schedule and optimizer fields from the native JSON are flattened too, including
`batch_size`, `seq_len`, `sample_every_steps`, `generate_tokens`,
`checkpoint_every_steps`, `schedule.warmup_steps`, `optimizer.learning_rate`,
and `optimizer.weight_decay`, so timing wrappers can show which values match
the long-run training profile and which cadences were deliberately disabled for
the benchmark window. Full `--train-transformer-lm` runtime JSON emits those
root fields plus nested `schedule` and `optimizer` objects, matching the
compiled plan contract instead of requiring callers to infer optimizer defaults
from the command line.
Arena families can be selected from the JSON without manual grouping. Main
transformer-LM global float buffers are named individually, for example
`mlp.fc.grad_out`, `attention.grad_out`, and `lm_head.float_logits`, instead of
being collapsed under a generic buffer label.
The native SM120 candidate wrapper defaults to 60 warmup pairs for
candidate-vs-current/reference runs and applies the same 60-pair floor to
long-run deferred-prewarm comparisons. The parity wrapper uses the same
60-pair long-run floor for current-vs-llm.kittens runs. Set
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_WARMUP=0`,
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_CANDIDATE_WARMUP=0`, or
`NFN_SM120_NATIVE_LONG_RUN_DEFER_PREWARM_MIN_WARMUP=0` only for intentional
cold-start diagnostics where first-use timing is the thing being measured.
Dry-run plans keep requested commands literal while reporting
`default_long_run_defer_prewarm_min_warmup_dry_run_would_apply` and
