For the TTT composite inner slice, use `nfn_ttt_llama_native_train --smoke-ttt-composite-inner-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model ttt-llama --native-cuda-smoke-ttt-composite-inner-step`; it launches base projection, down projection, tanh, up projection, residual add, latent MSE, full linear/tanh backward, and AdamW updates for all three weights through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the TTT full-transformer-loop slice, use `nfn_ttt_llama_native_train --smoke-ttt-full-transformer-loop-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model ttt-llama --native-cuda-smoke-ttt-full-transformer-loop-step`; it reports the composed base/down/tanh/up residual loss/backward/AdamW loop smoke through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the universal recurrent slice, use `nfn_universal_llama_native_train --smoke-universal-recurrent-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model universal-llama --native-cuda-smoke-universal-recurrent-step`; it launches recurrent linear forward, latent MSE, linear input/weight backward, and AdamW through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the universal ACT halt slice, use `nfn_universal_llama_native_train --smoke-universal-act-halt-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model universal-llama --native-cuda-smoke-universal-act-halt-step`; it launches halt-gate projection, Tile ACT halting BCE loss/gradient, ACT weighted-sum, linear backward, and AdamW through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the HNet byte patch slice, use `nfn_hnet_lm_native_train --smoke-hnet-byte-patch-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model hnet-lm --native-cuda-smoke-hnet-byte-patch-step`; it launches byte patch embed/merge, reconstruction head, latent MSE, linear head backward, and AdamW through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the HNet byte patch backward slice, use `nfn_hnet_lm_native_train --smoke-hnet-byte-patch-backward-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model hnet-lm --native-cuda-smoke-hnet-byte-patch-backward-step`; it launches merge backward, embed/projection backward, and AdamW through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the diffusion denoise slice, use `nfn_diffusion_native_train --smoke-diffusion-denoise-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model diffusion --native-cuda-smoke-diffusion-denoise-step`; it launches denoise linear forward, latent MSE, linear input/weight backward, and AdamW through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the diffusion objective slice, use `nfn_diffusion_native_train --smoke-diffusion-objective-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model diffusion --native-cuda-smoke-diffusion-objective-step`; it launches timestep sampling, mask scheduling, masked token embedding, token CE forward/backward, linear/embedding backward, and AdamW through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the diffusion full-loop slice, use `nfn_diffusion_native_train --smoke-diffusion-full-loop-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model diffusion --native-cuda-smoke-diffusion-full-loop-step`; it reports the timestep/mask/token-embedding/CE-backward/AdamW loop smoke through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the shared semantic hash/alignment slice, use `nfn_semantic_router_moe_native_train --smoke-semantic-alignment-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model semantic-router-moe --native-cuda-smoke-semantic-alignment-step`; it launches semantic hash and alignment loss-item kernels through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the semantic route-loss slice, use `nfn_semantic_router_moe_native_train --smoke-semantic-route-loss-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model semantic-router-moe --native-cuda-smoke-semantic-route-loss-step`; it launches route-selection loss, softmax distillation, and route-balance loss kernels through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls.

For the seq2seq loss-composition slice, use `nfn_seq2seq_native_train --smoke-seq2seq-loss-composition-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model seq2seq --native-cuda-smoke-seq2seq-loss-composition-step`; it runs decoder-to-encoder attention plus CE loss/backward and LM-head AdamW as the explicit no-Torch loss-composition coverage smoke.

For the seq2seq native dataset loop, use `nfn_seq2seq_native_train --train-seq2seq-dataset-loop --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model seq2seq --native-cuda-train-seq2seq-dataset-loop`; the bare seq2seq family command also defaults to this loop. It resolves native uint16 token shards, samples train and validation batches, runs the persistent encoder self-attention, decoder causal and cross-attention, stacked FFN, and token-CE Tile path without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow. Full-buffer Seq2seq gradients, stacked encoder/cross-QKV gradients, and norm-vector gradients accumulate directly into persistent optimizer buffers on device. Runtime and plan JSON report `kernel_step_source: "persistent_tile_seq2seq_full_geometry_forward_backward"`, `optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true`, `specialty_seq2seq_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, `specialty_seq2seq_stacked_qkv_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, `specialty_hnet_seq2seq_norm_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, and `specialty_direct_gradient_sync_elision: true`.

For the diffusion native dataset loop, use `nfn_diffusion_native_train --train-diffusion-dataset-loop --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model diffusion --native-cuda-train-diffusion-dataset-loop`; the bare diffusion family command also defaults to this loop. It resolves native uint16 token shards, samples train and validation batches, applies deterministic timestep masking, runs the full transformer denoising objective and token CE through the persistent CUDA Tile path, and writes the covered family checkpoint contract without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow. Runtime and plan JSON report `kernel_step_source: "persistent_tile_diffusion_full_geometry_forward_backward"` and `optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true`. Use `--train-diffusion-loop-step` only when you explicitly want the older one-shot composed train-step slice.

For the TTT native dataset loop, use `nfn_ttt_llama_native_train --train-ttt-dataset-loop --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model ttt-llama --native-cuda-train-ttt-dataset-loop`; the bare TTT family command also defaults to this loop. It resolves native uint16 token shards, samples train and validation batches, runs the persistent base/down/tanh/up inner update plus full transformer backbone and token CE through CUDA Tile without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow. Runtime and plan JSON report `kernel_step_source: "persistent_tile_ttt_full_geometry_forward_backward"`, `optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true`, `specialty_ttt_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, and `specialty_direct_gradient_sync_elision: true`.

For the LLaMA packed-QKV attention slice, use `nfn_llama_native_train --smoke-llama-packed-attention-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model llama --native-cuda-smoke-llama-packed-attention-step`; it launches packed-QKV BF16 causal attention with saved LSE and backward-to-QKV through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls. For the forward attention-block composition slice, use `nfn_llama_native_train --smoke-llama-attention-block-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model llama --native-cuda-smoke-llama-attention-block-step`; it composes RMSNorm, BF16 QKV projection, packed causal attention, BF16 unpack, and residual add without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow. For the RoPE attention-block integration slice, use `nfn_llama_native_train --smoke-llama-rope-attention-block-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model llama --native-cuda-smoke-llama-rope-attention-block-step`; it launches RMSNorm, QKV projection, head-major QKV split, RoPE, SDPA, and residual add through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls.

For the Jamba chunk-state slice, use `nfn_jamba_native_train --smoke-jamba-chunk-state-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model jamba --native-cuda-smoke-jamba-chunk-state-step`; it launches causal chunk-state, reconstruction head, latent MSE, linear head backward, and AdamW through raw CUDA Tile ABI calls.

For the Jamba native dataset loop, use `nfn_jamba_native_train --train-jamba-dataset-loop --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model jamba --native-cuda-train-jamba-dataset-loop`; the bare Jamba family command also defaults to this loop. It resolves native uint16 token shards, samples train and validation batches, runs sampled-token AR CE, then runs the composed Jamba layer-schedule CUDA Tile train-step slice without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow. Runtime and plan JSON report `kernel_step_source: "sampled_ar_ce_plus_jamba_layer_schedule_step"`, `optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true`, `specialty_jamba_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, and `specialty_direct_gradient_sync_elision: true`. Use `--train-jamba-loop-step` only when you explicitly want the older one-shot composed train-step slice.

For the composed seq2seq native train-step slice, use `nfn_seq2seq_native_train --train-seq2seq-loop-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model seq2seq --native-cuda-train-seq2seq-loop-step` when you explicitly want the older one-shot diagnostic. It wraps the full encoder-decoder loop smoke through compiled native C++ and reports substep JSON without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow.

For the composed diffusion native train-step slice, use `nfn_diffusion_native_train --train-diffusion-loop-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model diffusion --native-cuda-train-diffusion-loop-step` when you explicitly want the older one-shot diagnostic. It wraps the timestep/mask/objective loop smoke through compiled native C++ and reports substep JSON without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow.

For the composed TTT native train-step slice, use `nfn_ttt_llama_native_train --train-ttt-loop-step --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model ttt-llama --native-cuda-train-ttt-loop-step` when you explicitly want the older one-shot diagnostic. It wraps the full transformer loop smoke through compiled native C++ and reports substep JSON without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow.

For the HNet native byte dataset loop, use `nfn_hnet_lm_native_train --train-hnet-dataset-loop --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model hnet-lm --native-cuda-train-hnet-dataset-loop`; the bare HNet family command also defaults to this loop. It resolves native raw byte shards, samples train and validation byte batches, then runs the full HNet byte-patch transformer CUDA Tile train-step, including byte-vocabulary CE backward, without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow. Full-buffer HNet gradients and norm-vector gradients accumulate directly into persistent optimizer buffers on device. Runtime and plan JSON report `token_batch_source: "native_uint8_byte_shards"`, `kernel_step_source: "persistent_tile_hnet_byte_patch_full_geometry_forward_backward"`, `optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true`, `specialty_hnet_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, `specialty_hnet_seq2seq_norm_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, and `specialty_direct_gradient_sync_elision: true` when built with both production and full-geometry gates. Use `--train-hnet-loop-step` only when you explicitly want the older one-shot composed train-step slice.

For the universal-transformer native dataset loop, use `nfn_universal_llama_native_train --train-universal-dataset-loop --tile-ops-lib PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model universal-llama --native-cuda-train-universal-dataset-loop`; the bare universal-transformer family command also defaults to this loop. It resolves native uint16 token shards, samples train and validation batches, runs sampled-token AR CE, then runs the composed recurrent/ACT CUDA Tile train-step slice without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow. Runtime and plan JSON report `kernel_step_source: "sampled_ar_ce_plus_universal_transformer_loop_step"`, `optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true`, `specialty_universal_device_gradient_accumulation: true`, and `specialty_direct_gradient_sync_elision: true`. Use `--train-universal-loop-step` only when you explicitly want the older one-shot composed train-step slice.

For the shared family metadata slice, use `nfn_jepa_native_train --smoke-family-layout-checkpoint-step --output-dir PATH` or `nfn-native-train --base-model moe-jepa-evo --native-cuda-smoke-family-layout-checkpoint-step --native-cuda-output-dir PATH`; it emits the family parameter layout, writes native checkpoint metadata plus a `DONE` marker, writes a loadable native-family transition model plus deterministic dense-base/sampled-update `.f32` sidecar, and reports the native inference metadata contract without Torch or graph-editor tensor flow.

`cli/scripts/infer_gpt.py` is the canonical GPT inference entrypoint, with
`cli/scripts/infer_gpt2.py` kept as a compatibility wrapper. Both keep parser
construction, `--help`, and artifact default resolution lightweight. Importing
either module, running `python cli/scripts/infer_gpt.py --help`, or resolving
`--evo` / `--megakernel` defaults does not import Torch,
`server.dataset_manager`, or NumPy. Graph-backed `.pt` / `.json` generation
imports the runtime only after parsing; native `.bin` checkpoint prompts
call the SDK `run_native_gpt_checkpoint_sampler()` helper, which prefers the
C++ capture binding and falls back to the compiled
`nfn_gpt_native_train --sample-checkpoint` path when needed. The wrapper
forwards `--temperature`, `--top-k`, `--repetition-penalty`, and `--seed` to
the native sampler instead of silently using greedy-only generation.
Explicit `--runtime native-cuda` inference fails fast for graph `.pt/.json`
artifacts so the CLI cannot silently fall through to the graph-backed
chat/runtime path after the user requested native CUDA.
The canonical wrapper preserves its own argparse program name, so
`python cli/scripts/infer_gpt.py --help` prints `usage: infer_gpt.py`; the
compatibility `infer_gpt2.py` name is reserved for direct compatibility-script
execution.

## Native artifact serving

`nfn infer --checkpoint ARTIFACT --serve` routes through the lightweight CLI
before one-shot native checkpoint detection or graph-backed `nfn_impl` import.
Install the dedicated dependencies first:

```bash
pip install -e '.[serve]'
nfn infer \
  --checkpoint artifacts/model-native \
  --serve \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 8000 \
  --served-model-name my-model \
  --session-limit 9 \
  --chat-template plain_roles \
  --kv-cache auto \
  --state-db ./native-inference-state.sqlite3 \
  --prefix-cache-capacity 64
```

Serving accepts only a Native Execution artifact whose manifest and in-process
binding jointly prove resident ABI v1. Before Uvicorn binds, startup validates
the tokenizer, supported chat renderer, positive context limit, contained
checkpoint path, requested cache capability, and remote-auth policy. The
current dense-v5 CPU reference binding defaults `auto` to its preallocated
lossless full cache; explicit `full` selects the same cache, `off` selects
full-prefix recomputation, and `turboquant` selects the jointly proved native
packed CPU cache. Unsupported artifacts and head geometry fail closed.
For a compatible reviewed-dense artifact, add
`--turboquant-attention-backend tile-cuda --tile-ops-lib
/absolute/path/libnfn_native_train_tile_ops_strict.so` (plus optional
`--cuda-runtime-lib` and `--cuda-device`) to move compressed historical
attention to CUDA. CPU remains the default and an explicit request never falls
back.
Canonical LLaMA uses the same resident ABI with `auto`/`full`/`off` and rejects
TurboQuant. Its raw-token CLI path does not imply text serving: startup still
requires an artifact-declared supported tiktoken codec and chat renderer.

Useful flags:

- `--queue-capacity N` bounds waiting generations in front of one compute worker.
- `--session-limit N` bounds all admitted request-session reservations, including the running generation and queued work. It defaults to `queue_capacity + 1`; saturation returns `session_limit_exceeded` rather than blocking.
- `--max-output-tokens N` sets the server request ceiling (default 256). When a
  Responses request omits `max_output_tokens`, constrained schema/forced-call
  generation defaults to `min(256, ceiling)` while ordinary text and the
  function-result continuation default to `min(16, ceiling)`.
- `--chat-template auto|plain_roles|PATH` selects artifact metadata or an explicit fallback; template files contain the literal `{messages}` placeholder.
- `--api-key-file PATH` or `NFN_INFER_API_KEY` enables Bearer auth on every route.
- `--state-db PATH` enables the private WAL-backed Responses/Conversations store, restart-safe background jobs, and resumable background-stream event ledger.
- `--prefix-cache-capacity N` retains at most `N` sealed foreground Responses
  sessions in a process-local deterministic LRU. It defaults to `0`, requires
  `--state-db`, and accepts only proven full-cache COW or reviewed dense CPU
  TurboQuant COW. Tile-CUDA is rejected while this option is positive.
- `--allow-unauthenticated-remote` explicitly overrides the rule that a non-loopback host must have a key.
- `--turboquant-profile mse-3.5|qjl-3.5` selects the explicit compressed profile and becomes effective only with joint artifact/binding/cache-ABI proof.
- `--turboquant-attention-backend cpu|tile-cuda` selects CPU by default; the
  Tile option additionally requires `--tile-ops-lib PATH` and the separate
  strict feature ABI. `--cuda-runtime-lib` and `--cuda-device` pin runtime and
  device when needed.

The state file is schema v4. It retains typed function-call/result history and
adds a monotonic conversation-item revision for snapshot/CAS completion.
Opening an existing v1/v2/v3 file adds the revision in place and treats prior
history as revision zero. Back up the file before first use with this version
if rollback matters; older binaries reject v4. A conversation-linked
background response queued by an older binary has no historical revision
snapshot to migrate and is terminalized as failed with
`conversation_snapshot_unavailable` rather than running against current items.
A legacy previous-response-only job reconstructs only a currently
completed/incomplete lineage or fails with `response_lineage_unavailable`.

The isolated app exposes `/health`, model list/retrieve, and bounded OpenAI
Chat Completions. Chat is text by default; a jointly proven CPU or whole-model
CUDA Muse Glimmer vision artifact also accepts base64 image data URLs. SSE emits committed-token `chat.completion.chunk` records and
terminates with `data: [DONE]`. With `--state-db`, it also exposes the bounded
text Responses and Conversations resources, API-key-scoped lineage, semantic
Responses SSE, local response compaction, and durable background/cancel
processing. A response created with `background: true`, `stream: true`, and
`store: true` continues after its subscriber disconnects and can be replayed
strictly after a saved `sequence_number` with
`GET /v1/responses/{id}?stream=true&starting_after=N`; replay includes persisted
delta obfuscation unless `include_obfuscation=false` is requested. When the
artifact/binding/tokenizer jointly prove the exact constrained profiles and
`--chat-template auto` selects the artifact presentation, Responses also accept
stored buffered foreground strict flat JSON-schema output and one forced
client-executed function call plus its later string result. NeuralFn never
executes that function. General/parallel/hosted tools, nested/array schemas,
constrained streams/background work, Chat Completions tools, Responses
multimedia, audio/files/server-video, logprobs, penalties, and unimplemented
`/v1` resources return OpenAI-shaped capability errors rather than being
ignored.

With prefix capacity enabled, a foreground `previous_response_id` or
conversation request can fork the exact verified rendered-token LCP. Only
stored completed/incomplete responses publish after durable completion;
failed, cancelled, non-stored, and background work does not enter the cache.
`store: false` may hit but cannot admit, Chat and background stay cold, and a
restart has no resident cache entries. Usage reports native-bounded exact-LCP
`cached_tokens` and prompt-only `cache_write_tokens`, never decoded rows.
`/health.prefix_cache` exposes LRU and capacity-observation counters; its byte
values may double-represent COW-shared allocations and are not physical
process memory. Response/conversation/item deletion purges the whole API-key
scope. Keep one owning server/service process per cache-enabled state database;
out-of-band store mutations cannot notify the process-local fence. A racing
conversation mutation produces `conversation_conflict` (buffered 409 or a
semantic failed terminal for already-open stream/background work). Every
`previous_response_id` lineage is re-read at terminalization; deleted or changed
ancestry produces `response_lineage_conflict` before output/cache publication.
Shutdown awaits the background driver and tracked foreground stream drivers,
drains the queue, then closes cache, model, and state in that order. See
[Native Inference Serving](rest-api/native-inference-serving.md).

## Datasets and tokenizers

Dataset shortcuts are resolved by the shared selector logic in
`cli/scripts/train_jepa_semantic.py`.

| Shortcut | Data path | Default tokenizer |
|----------|-----------|-------------------|
| `golf1` | cached-token parameter-golf, one training shard | `sp1024` |
| `golf10` | cached-token parameter-golf, ten training shards | `sp1024` |
| `shakespeare` / `shakespear` | raw text | `cl100k_base` |
| `tinystories` | raw text from TinyStoriesV2 GPT-4 files | `o200k_base` |
| `--pretraining-file FILE` | local raw `.txt` file | tokenizer selected by `--tokenizer` or dataset defaults |

Tokenizers are separate from datasets. `--tokenizer` accepts
`gpt2`, `cl100k_base`, `o200k_base`, `sp1024`, `sp2048`, `sp4096`, and
`sp8192`. SentencePiece assets live under `~/.cache/nfn/tokenizers`; if a
cached dataset already contains matching tokenizer files under its
`tokenizers/` directory, the CLI promotes them into the shared tokenizer cache
before trying a download.

The GPT-2 compatibility training wrapper accepts the same pretraining-file and
dataset shortcut flags for parser/API compatibility without importing Torch.
Direct script execution still dispatches to compiled native GPT training before
loading those compatibility helpers.

Missing cached dataset aliases are downloaded by default when the CLI can
derive a contract from the alias or explicit download flags. Existing aliases
remain strict: tokenizer-backed shard/vocab mismatches fail fast and should be
fixed by rebuilding or re-downloading the alias.

Raw-text aliases avoid repeated graph/editor data movement. Schedule estimation
uses `meta.json` token counts or cached shard sizes when available. When the
selected tokenizer fits in `uint16` (`gpt2` and the current SentencePiece
variants), the first training load writes `fineweb_train_000000.bin` and optional
`fineweb_val_000000.bin` beside `data.txt` / `val.txt`; later runs memmap those
shards instead of re-tokenizing raw text. Tokenizers with ids outside `uint16`,
such as `o200k_base`, stay on the raw-text path.

## Artifacts

By default, the CLI writes to `~/NeuralFn/artifacts`. Set
`NEURALFN_ARTIFACTS_DIR` to override that shared artifact root for CLI and
server graph-run outputs.

Training saves:

- `<mode>.pt` for weights
- `<mode>.json` for the exported graph
- `<mode>.interrupted.pt` and `<mode>.interrupted.json` when interrupted

The graph JSON records `artifact_metadata.weights_file`, tokenizer metadata,
and training metadata so inference can load graph-first and treat `--weights`
as an override.

`nfn infer` also has a graphless compatibility path for flat Parameter Golf
root-GPT `.pt` checkpoints. Use `--checkpoint` with the matching SentencePiece
`.model` file, and optionally pass the training log so non-tensor hints can be
read from its `Hyperparameters` block:

```bash
nfn infer \
  --checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/final_model.pt \
  --checkpoint-tokenizer ~/Downloads/fineweb_8192_bpe_lossless_caps_caseops_v1_reserved.model \
  --checkpoint-log ~/Downloads/a54a53b3-7d6e-461c-975a-590030e61bd0.txt
```

Passing `--weights <checkpoint>.pt` without `--graph` routes to the same
graphless loader. NeuralFn graph exports remain the primary format and should
continue to use `--graph`.

Native GPT CUDA checkpoints from `train_gpt2cu` or NeuralFn native dense GPT
training are recognized separately from graph-backed `.pt` artifacts. Inspect
them without importing Torch:

```bash
nfn infer --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --native-info
python cli/scripts/infer_gpt.py --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --native-info
nfn_gpt_native_train --native-info --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin
nfn_gpt_native_train --inspect-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin
nfn infer --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --max-new-tokens 16
nfn infer --runtime native-cuda --checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --max-new-tokens 16
nfn_gpt_native_train --sample-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --max-new-tokens 16
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-logits-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-qkv-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --checkpoint-block-index 0
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-attention-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --checkpoint-block-index 0
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-attention-residual-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --checkpoint-block-index 0
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-block-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --checkpoint-block-index 0
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-block-logits-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3 --checkpoint-block-index 0
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-forward-logits-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --prompt-tokens 1,2,3
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-load-smoke --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin --checkpoint-load-tensor h.0.ln_1.weight --checkpoint-load-elements 1024
nfn_gpt_native_train --checkpoint-layout --native-checkpoint ~/NeuralFn/artifacts/gpt2/model_00020000.bin
```

To prove dense GPT checkpoint loadability for every covered dense selector, use:

```bash
python tools/smoke_native_gpt_template_checkpoints.py \
  --native-bin build/nfn_gpt_native_train \
  --output-dir /tmp/nfn-native-dense-gpt-sweep \
  --json
```

The sweep writes an isolated sparse native checkpoint for each dense selector and
then runs `nfn_gpt_native_train --native-info --native-checkpoint ...` against
that artifact. The checkpoint metadata smoke uses the selected template geometry:
NanoGPT-family outputs report `layers=5 heads=5 channels=320`, while GPT-2,
GPT-2 MoA/megakernel/modern, GPT, and GPT-3 selectors report
`layers=12 heads=12 channels=768`. The sweep parses the literal preset
declarations without importing optional NumPy-backed SDK modules.

`gpt2_moa` is a live native training mode, not only a selector alias. The
compiled transformer loop evaluates GELU, ReLU, SiLU, and ReLU2 on the same
training batch at step 1 and every `--native-cuda-moa-interval` steps, chooses
the lowest-loss candidate, and uses it for backward/update on the shared MLP
weights. Runtime JSON exposes `moa_selected_activation`, `moa_probe_runs`,
`moa_candidate_evals`, and `moa_last_probe_losses`. MoA training opts out of
lazy validation-only MLP float scratch because its training probes need the split
`fc_out`/activation buffers; the Tile BF16 GELU fallback kernels accept no-bias
probe calls with null bias pointers.

For a graph-authored production run, completion is the source-bound
`model_XXXXXXXX.moa.json` beside its named dense-v5 `.bin` and empty DONE
marker, not the bare model. The metadata records the canonical candidates,
selected activation, positive interval, and exact graph/model hashes. Resume
requires that same sidecar, restores its activation without a fresh probe, and
fails closed when the metadata is missing or changed. Direct selector-only
`--template-name gpt2_moa` first-leg training still writes ordinary dense-v5,
but that unbound output cannot be resumed activation-faithfully.

This reports the native header shape, precision, expected size, and `DONE_*`
marker state. The compiled `nfn_gpt_native_train` forms emit JSON and return
before CUDA, token-shard resolution, Torch, Python dataset setup, or graph-node
execution. The prompt-token forms dispatch to compiled C++ and validate the
checkpoint, context window, vocab bounds, and token list without Torch or
graph-node flow, then execute autoregressive CUDA Tile checkpoint forward passes
and return up to `--max-new-tokens` IDs in `generated_tokens`. Text prompt
generation from native `.bin` checkpoints now tokenizes with the GPT-2 tokenizer
in the lightweight wrapper and then uses the same compiled sampler path; the
wrapper reprints the compiled JSON and then prints generated token IDs plus
GPT-2-decoded generated text. The graph-backed chat path will not attempt to load
native `.bin` files as Torch checkpoints.

Covered native-family dataset loops also emit a lightweight JSON checkpoint
next to their loop metadata: `*_native_family_model_00000000.json` plus a
matching `*_native_family_model_DONE` marker. These checkpoints are produced by
the compiled C++ family trainers from the sampled native token or byte batches
and are recognized by the lightweight `nfn infer` path before `nfn_impl`, Torch,
NumPy, tokenizers, dataset managers, or graph-backed runtime modules load:

```bash
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts/dense_jepa_native_family_model_00000000.json --native-info
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts/dense_jepa_native_family_model_00000000.json --verify
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts --verify-all
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts --verify-all --required-templates dense-jepa-evo-modern,llama-modern
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts --verify-all --require-covered-templates
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts --verify-all --require-covered-templates --require-architecture-forward
nfn infer --checkpoint artifacts/dense_jepa_native_family_model_00000000.json --prompt-tokens 50256,464 --max-new-tokens 64
```

Current optimizer-updated native-family artifacts use
`nfn-native-family-optimizer-checkpoint-v1`; `nfn infer` also accepts the older
`nfn-native-family-token-transition-v1` transition artifacts. Both are real
loadable models so covered native templates produce an inference artifact
immediately, and current optimizer artifacts also record
`architecture_parameter_layout`, `native_parameter_state`, and `parameter_data`
for the full-size float32 sidecar. Current diagnostic checkpoints label that
state as `optimizer_updated_dense_float32_parameter_state`: `nfn infer`
validates the dense sidecar size and can score bounded candidates through the
`token_embedding_lm_head_sidecar_forward` path. The C++ writer patches sampled
token or byte gradients into the full contiguous family layout, runs
`nfn_native_tile_adamw_step_float32`, persists the updated `.f32` sidecar, and
records `optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: false`.
That is a loadable sampled-sidecar artifact, not full optimizer-updated dense
tensor persistence; family JSON continues to report that production gap until
every architecture parameter is optimizer-updated and persisted.
For explicit production-loop builds where `NFN_NATIVE_PRODUCTION_LOOP=1` and
the production bootstrap is ready, checkpoint metadata may report
`live_family_device_parameter_store_float32_state` and
`optimizer_updated_full_architecture_parameter_persistence: true` only when
`NFN_NATIVE_FULL_GEOMETRY_FORWARD_BACKWARD=1` is also set; the live-store path
copies the `FamilyDeviceParameterStore` sidecar after the shared
`FamilyOptimizerState` step. Architecture-forward inference support remains
false until a real family forward path consumes those persistent parameters.
`--native-info` is a metadata read; `--verify` is the stricter loadability gate
that requires the model `DONE` marker, matching sidecar byte size, nonempty
transition state, full-template parameter state, contiguous buffer layout,
trained sidecar slots, the checkpoint writer's own sidecar readback
verification block, and a bounded successful sample. When `--checkpoint` points
at an output directory, `--verify` checks the latest native-family model
checkpoint in that directory. Use `--verify-all` to check every
`*_native_family_model_*.json` artifact in the directory and return one summary
JSON payload with per-checkpoint pass/fail results. Add
`--required-templates TEMPLATE[,TEMPLATE...]` to require checkpoint coverage for
a named subset, or `--require-covered-templates` to require every template alias
in the native-family registry plus each direct native-family checkpoint target.
The coverage gate keys off each checkpoint's normalized `template_name`, so a
family-level smoke artifact proves only the template it records and does not
silently cover all aliases mapped to the same family binary.
Add `--require-architecture-forward` when a gate must prove architecture-forward
inference from the persisted parameter state rather than falling back to the
transition sampler or the LM-head-only path. Full live-parameter checkpoints
that record `trained_parameter_elements == parameter_elements` can pass this
gate; diagnostic `token_embedding_lm_head_sidecar_forward` artifacts
intentionally fail it.
Native-family model filenames are template-aware: when `--template-name` names
an alias, the C++ writer prefixes the model JSON, `.f32` sidecar, and model
`DONE` marker with the sanitized template name before the family prefix. This
lets a sweep run repeated alias smokes into one `--output-dir` and then use the
coverage gate without later aliases overwriting earlier family artifacts.
To produce that sweep from already built family binaries, run:

```bash
tools/smoke_native_family_template_checkpoints.py \
  --native-bin-dir build \
  --output-dir artifacts/native-family-template-smoke \
  --json
```

Pass `--templates dense-jepa-evo-modern,llama-modern` to limit the sweep. The
tool maps each template to its native-family binary, runs
`--smoke-family-layout-checkpoint-step --template-name TEMPLATE`, and then
verifies the output directory with the covered-template audit. `--json` omits
successful smoke stdout/stderr by default to keep CI logs bounded; add
`--include-smoke-output` for failure bisection. The sweep tool also accepts
`--require-architecture-forward` for the same stricter production-readiness gate.
The missing-family trainer build script defaults to optimized `-O3`; set
`NFN_NATIVE_MISSING_CXX_OPT_FLAGS=-O0` when you need a bounded local rebuild for
checkpoint-writing or CLI verification rather than release-binary benchmarking.

For native GPT training, `--eval-every-steps 0` disables validation and the
compiled C++ token resolver does not require or stat validation shards. Plan and
runtime JSON report `validation_shards_required` and
`validation_shards_resolved`, so train-only cached shard directories are
distinguishable from validation-capable runs.

`--checkpoint-load-smoke` is the compiled CUDA prerequisite check for that
sampler: it reads a bounded bf16 payload slice from the checkpoint, copies it to
device memory, converts it with `nfn_native_tile_bf16_bits_to_float32`, and
verifies copyback without Torch, token-shard resolution, Python datasets, or
graph-editor tensors. Pass `--checkpoint-load-tensor NAME` to seek to a named
tensor using the decoded checkpoint layout before copying the slice.
`--checkpoint-layout` is the no-CUDA companion for sampler wiring: it decodes
the header-derived tensor layout, payload offsets, file offsets, and bounded
payload samples as compiled C++ JSON.
`--checkpoint-logits-smoke` is the first checkpoint-backed CUDA forward slice:
it loads checkpoint embeddings and final norm tensors, converts bf16 weights on
device, and runs token embedding, position embedding, residual add, final
LayerNorm, and tied LM-head logits for the last prompt token. It does not yet
execute transformer blocks.
`--checkpoint-qkv-smoke` advances that path into a selected transformer block:
it loads `wte.weight`, `wpe.weight`, `h.N.ln_1.weight`, `h.N.ln_1.bias`,
`h.N.attn.c_attn.weight`, and `h.N.attn.c_attn.bias`, converts them on device,
and runs embedding residual, block LayerNorm, and QKV projection through CUDA
Tile kernels. Use `--checkpoint-block-index N` to select the block. It still
does not execute attention, MLP, or the generation loop.
`--checkpoint-attention-smoke` continues that same checkpoint-backed block stage
through split-to-heads, causal scaled-dot-product attention, and merge-heads on
CUDA Tile kernels. It still stops before attention output projection, residual
add, MLP, and generation-loop sampling.
`--checkpoint-attention-residual-smoke` loads `h.N.attn.c_proj.weight` and
`h.N.attn.c_proj.bias`, then runs the attention output projection and residual
add on CUDA Tile kernels. It still stops before `ln_2`, MLP, and generation-loop
sampling.
`--checkpoint-block-smoke` continues through `ln_2`, MLP fc, GELU+bias, MLP
projection, and the final block residual add on CUDA Tile kernels. It still
stops before final LayerNorm, tied LM-head logits, and generation-loop sampling.
`--checkpoint-block-logits-smoke` continues through final LayerNorm and tied
LM-head logits for the last prompt token, reporting top token/logit metadata.
It still runs only the selected checkpoint block rather than a multi-layer
forward loop.
`--checkpoint-forward-logits-smoke` runs every checkpoint GPT block in order,
then final LayerNorm and the tied LM head for the last prompt token. It reports
`transformer_blocks_executed: true`, `blocks_executed`, and
`graph_editor_node_flow: false`; generation-loop sampling is still the remaining
native inference step.

For flat Parameter Golf checkpoints, architecture comes from tensor shapes plus
compatible metadata. A supplied training log may provide safe runtime hints
such as context window or logit softcap, but newer experimental structural
hints are ignored when the tensors are not present in the checkpoint. CaseOps
SentencePiece models use display cleanup that hides private-use case markers
and suppresses reconstruction-only tokens during sampling, including byte
fallback, ellipsis artifacts, and the high-id single-character fallback band
that can otherwise look like masked or gapped output in chat.

Graphless Parameter Golf sampling uses a conservative repeat guard by default:
`--no-repeat-ngram-size 4`, `--repeat-run-limit 3`, and the balanced
repetition-penalty preset. Lower `--no-repeat-ngram-size` to `3` or raise the
chat setting with `/repeat 1.15` when a checkpoint drifts into repeated
punctuation or phrase loops.

In interactive `nfn infer`, slash completion is live. A buffer beginning with
`/` shows matching commands in the status line as you type; unique prefixes
complete in place on Tab, ambiguous prefixes list matches, and value commands
show their expected argument after the command name. `/autocomplete n` enables
inline typing predictions for `n` words. The predicted text is rendered as a
50% gray ghost suffix after the cursor. The suffix preserves the model's
generated word boundary: a leading space starts a new word, and no leading
space completes the current word. Tab accepts the visible prediction. Use
`/autocomplete 0` to disable inline predictions and return non-command prompts
to the token-preview behavior: press Tab once to preview the next token and Tab
again to insert it when safe. Wrapped prompts and ghost predictions are
repainted as a full multi-row block so stale rows are cleared as the input
changes.

## Presets

The CLI includes a preset stack for the supplied lossless-caps Parameter Golf
training run:

```bash
nfn train \
  --model-preset parameter_golf_caseops_8192 \
  --run-preset parameter_golf_10min \
  --optimizer-preset parameter_golf_muon \
  --tokenizer sp8192
```

When `parameter_golf_caseops_8192` is selected, the planner recommends
`parameter_golf_10min`, `parameter_golf_muon`, and `sp8192` unless those values
were passed explicitly.

## Fine-tuning flags

`nfn train` can build fine-tuning root graphs through the same recipe path:

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--training-mode sft` | Supervised fine-tuning with `sft_dataset_source` and masked token CE. |
| `--training-mode dpo` | Direct Preference Optimization with policy/reference forwards. |
| `--training-mode ppo` | PPO inner graph plus real `PPOTrainer` rollout/reference/reward/KL/GAE orchestration. |
| `--training-mode reward_model` | Preference reward-head training. |
| `--adapter-type lora` | Insert trainable LoRA projections. |
| `--adapter-type qlora` | Use nf4 base projection buffers plus LoRA deltas. |
| `--adapter-type randmap` | Use fixed random projections with a trainable middle adapter. |
| `--adapter-only-save` | Save only adapter/head parameters after training. |

Fine-tuning checkpoints use `--base-checkpoint`, `--ref-checkpoint`, and
`--reward-checkpoint` depending on the selected objective.

## Verification

Useful non-training checks:

```bash
conda run -n NeuralFn python cli/nfn.py --help
conda run -n NeuralFn python cli/nfn.py train --help
conda run -n NeuralFn python -m pytest cli/tests/test_nfn_cli.py -q
conda run -n NeuralFn python -m pytest cli/tests/test_train_pretraining_file_flags.py -q
```

Training jobs are CUDA-oriented and may be long-running; use the smoke
`--run-preset` or targeted unit tests for local doc/API verification.

Native diffusion full-geometry plans now size `denoise_head.weight` as a
`model_dim -> vocab_size` projection and use token cross-entropy for the
denoise objective. The corresponding path applies deterministic
timestep-driven masking before embedding and collects denoiser and
input-embedding gradients. Normal diffusion builds enable production and full
geometry; CUDA execution still requires the family Tile ABI and a usable CUDA
driver.
